textes.Les éléments, les liaisons, les acides e: Elements, bonds, acids and bases, reactions.
textes.Démocrite d'Abdère, à la suite de son ma: Democritus of Abdera, following his teacher Leucippus, claims that everything is made of tiny, indivisible particles moving in the void: atoms, from the Greek atomos, “uncuttable.” With no experiment to show it, it is a philosophical intuition. It took John Dalton, around 1808, for an atomic theory based on measurements, then Einstein (1905) and Jean Perrin (1908) for atoms to become indisputable.
textes.Démocrite a eu raison 2 300 ans trop tôt: Democritus was right 2,300 years too early. In science, that's almost worse than being wrong.
textes.Démocrite imaginait des atomes insécable: Democritus imagined unbreakable atoms, hooked or smooth, of all shapes. There are a hundred and eighteen kinds, and none is unbreakable. A wild atom comes out of the void to tell him so.
textes.Lavoisier et la masse qui se conserve: Lavoisier and the conservation of mass
textes.Antoine Lavoisier publie le Traité éléme: Antoine Lavoisier published the Elementary Treatise on Chemistry. By weighing everything, before and after each reaction, he showed that mass is conserved. He explained combustion by oxygen and buried the phlogiston theory. His wife, Marie-Anne Paulze, translated English works, kept the laboratory notebooks and engraved the treatise's plates.
textes.« Rien ne se perd, rien ne se crée » : L: “Nothing is lost, nothing is created”: Lavoisier didn't write that sentence word for word. But you don't lose this turn.
textes.Lavoisier était aussi fermier général, c: Lavoisier was also a tax farmer, that is, a tax collector. Arrested during the Terror, he was guillotined on May 8, 1794. The phrase attributed to the judge, “The Republic has no need of scientists,” is probably a legend: he most likely never said it. Lagrange is said to have remarked that it took only an instant to cut off that head, and a hundred years might not be enough to produce another like it.
textes.Retour au début de l'époque. Vous gardez: Back to the start of the era. You keep your head, which is already better than Lavoisier.
textes.Dmitri Mendeleïev range les 63 éléments: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the 63 known elements by mass and properties, and left empty squares for unknown elements whose properties he predicted. Gallium (1875), scandium (1879) and germanium (1886) came to fill them. According to a story he told himself, the table came to him in a dream.
textes.63 éléments connus en 1869, 63 cases ici: 63 elements known in 1869, 63 squares here. Coincidence? Yes. The AI is not superstitious.
textes.Mendeleïev laisse des cases vides pour d: Mendeleev left empty squares for elements not yet known, and predicted their properties. Gallium proved him right in 1875. An atom comes out of its square.
textes.Marie et Pierre Curie découvrent le polo: Marie and Pierre Curie discovered polonium, named after Marie's native Poland, then radium. Marie Curie was the first woman Nobel laureate (physics, 1903) and remains the only person awarded in two different sciences (chemistry, 1911). Her notebooks are still radioactive: the Bibliothèque nationale de France keeps her manuscripts in lead-lined boxes.
textes.Ses carnets sont radioactifs depuis plus: Her notebooks have been radioactive for more than a century. Your revision notes have a half-life of about two days.
textes.Marie et Pierre Curie traitent des tonne: Marie and Pierre Curie processed tons of pitchblende to isolate a few decigrams of radium. Here, one wild atom will do.
textes.La structure de l'atome, les éléments et: The structure of the atom, the elements and the periodic table.
textes.Un atome : un noyau (protons et neutrons: An atom: a nucleus (protons and neutrons) with electrons around it.
textes.Le numéro atomique (nombre de protons) d: The atomic number (number of protons) defines the element.
textes.Le tableau périodique range les éléments: The periodic table arranges the elements by number; a column groups similar chemical properties.
textes.Un atome est presque vide : si le noyau: An atom is almost empty: if the nucleus were a marble, the atom would be the size of a stadium.
textes.Changer le nombre de neutrons donne un i: Changing the number of neutrons gives an isotope of the same element, not another element.
textes.Comment les atomes s'assemblent : liaiso: How atoms join together: covalent and ionic bonds, polarity.
textes.Liaison covalente : deux atomes partagen: Covalent bond: two atoms share a pair of electrons (H₂O, CH₄).
textes.Liaison ionique : un atome cède un élect: Ionic bond: one atom gives an electron to the other; the ions attract each other (NaCl).
textes.Une molécule est polaire si les charges: A molecule is polar if its charges are unevenly distributed: water is, hence its properties as a solvent.
textes.Les liaisons hydrogène entre molécules d: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules explain its high boiling point.
textes.La glace flotte parce que ses liaisons h: Ice floats because its hydrogen bonds arrange it in a more open lattice than liquid water.
textes.pH < 7 : acide ; pH = 7 : neutre ; pH >: pH < 7: acidic; pH = 7: neutral; pH > 7: basic.
textes.L'échelle est logarithmique : pH 3 est d: The scale is logarithmic: pH 3 is ten times more acidic than pH 4.
textes.Une baisse d'une unité de pH n'est pas u: A drop of one pH unit is not a small change: it means ten times more H⁺ ions.
textes.Échelle de pH de 0 à 14 : acide, neutre,: pH scale from 0 to 14: acidic, neutral, basic
textes.Équations, combustion, catalyse, oxydati: Equations, combustion, catalysis, oxidation and reduction.
textes.Une équation chimique doit être équilibr: A chemical equation must be balanced: the same number of atoms of each kind on both sides (Lavoisier).
textes.Combustion : un combustible + du dioxygè: Combustion: a fuel + oxygen → CO₂, water and heat.
textes.Un catalyseur accélère une réaction sans: A catalyst speeds up a reaction without being consumed. Oxidation: loss of electrons; reduction: gain.
textes.La rouille n'est pas une simple « saleté: Rust is not just “dirt”: it is oxidized iron, bulkier, which cracks the metal.
textes.Une équation équilibrée : 4 H et 2 O de: A balanced equation: 4 H and 2 O on each side
textes.Solide, liquide, gaz, changements d'état: Solid, liquid, gas, changes of state and the gas laws.
textes.Solide, liquide, gaz : même matière, agi: Solid, liquid, gas: the same matter, with different agitation and distance between molecules.
textes.Fusion, vaporisation, condensation, soli: Melting, vaporization, condensation, solidification, sublimation (solid → gas), deposition (gas → solid).
textes.Pendant un changement d'état, la tempéra: During a change of state, the temperature stays constant.
textes.À volume fixé, la pression d'un gaz augm: At fixed volume, the pressure of a gas rises with temperature (PV = nRT).
textes.L'eau bout à moins de 100 °C en altitude: Water boils below 100 °C at altitude: about 70 °C at the top of Everest.
textes.Le carbone, les hydrocarbures, les polym: Carbon, hydrocarbons, polymers and the molecules of life.
textes.La chimie organique est celle des compos: Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds; carbon forms four bonds.
textes.Hydrocarbures : uniquement carbone et hy: Hydrocarbons: only carbon and hydrogen (methane, butane, octane).
textes.Polymères : longues chaînes d'unités rép: Polymers: long chains of repeating units (polyethylene, DNA, cellulose).
textes.Les glucides, lipides, protéines et acid: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids are the great molecules of life.
textes.« Chimique » ne s'oppose pas à « naturel: “Chemical” is not the opposite of “natural”: everything alive is made of organic molecules.
textes.Un polymère : une chaîne de petites unit: A polymer: a chain of small units
textes.Cuisine, savon, médicaments, piles et ma: Cooking, soap, medicines, batteries and materials.
textes.Le savon a une tête qui aime l'eau et un: Soap has a head that likes water and a tail that likes grease: it traps grease in micelles.
textes.La réaction de Maillard (sucres + protéi: The Maillard reaction (sugars + proteins with heat) browns bread and sears meat.
textes.Une pile transforme une réaction d'oxydo: A battery turns a redox reaction into a current.
textes.Le paracétamol et l'aspirine sont des mo: Paracetamol and aspirin are synthetic molecules; aspirin derives from willow bark.
textes.Mélanger eau de Javel et vinaigre dégage: Mixing bleach and vinegar releases toxic chlorine: never combine household products.
textes.Isotopes, demi-vie, fission, fusion et d: Isotopes, half-life, fission, fusion and dating.
textes.Demi-vie : le temps pour que la moitié d: Half-life: the time for half of the radioactive nuclei to decay. It does not depend on the quantity.
textes.Le carbone 14 (demi-vie ≈ 5 730 ans) dat: Carbon-14 (half-life ≈ 5,730 years) dates organic remains up to about 50,000 years.
textes.Fission : un noyau lourd se casse (centr: Fission: a heavy nucleus splits (power plants). Fusion: light nuclei join (the Sun).
textes.α arrêté par une feuille de papier, β pa: α is stopped by a sheet of paper, β by a few millimeters of aluminum, γ by lead or thick concrete.
textes.Après deux demi-vies, il ne reste pas zé: After two half-lives, what remains is not zero but a quarter.
textes.pH = −log[H⁺] : 10⁻³ mol/L d'ions H⁺ don: pH = −log[H⁺]: 10⁻³ mol/L of H⁺ ions gives a pH of 3, 10⁻⁷ gives 7.
textes.Une mole de gaz parfait à 0 °C sous une: One mole of ideal gas at 0 °C and one atmosphere takes up about 22.4 L.
textes.Un noyau minuscule dans beaucoup de vide: A tiny nucleus in a lot of emptiness
textes.Protons et neutrons dans le noyau, élect: Protons and neutrons in the nucleus, electrons around it. The nucleus carries almost all the mass, but the atom is mostly empty space (Rutherford, 1911).
textes.Un atome, c'est un noyau, fait de proton: An atom is a nucleus, made of protons and neutrons, surrounded by electrons. Almost all of its mass is in the nucleus, and yet the nucleus is tiny: the atom is 27,000 to 60,000 times wider, depending on the element. If the nucleus were a marble, the atom would be the size of a stadium.
textes.On l'a compris en tirant dessus. Entre 1: We found out by shooting at it. Between 1906 and 1913, in Manchester, Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden fired alpha particles at a very thin gold foil, under Ernest Rutherford's direction. Almost all went straight through, but a few bounced back. In 1911 Rutherford drew the conclusion: the positive charge and the mass are packed into a very small centre, the nucleus.
textes.Le numéro qui fait l'élément: The number that makes the element
textes.Protons = identité de l'élément. Neutron: Protons = the element's identity. More or fewer neutrons = isotope. More or fewer electrons = ion.
textes.Les neutrons, eux, peuvent varier sans c: Neutrons can vary without changing the element: that gives isotopes. Carbon-12 and carbon-14 both have 6 protons; the second has two more neutrons. Electrons can vary too: an atom that gains or loses some becomes a charged ion, like Na⁺ or Cl⁻ in salt.
textes.Une colonne du tableau = une famille aux: A column of the table = a family with similar properties. Mendeleev (1869) predicted missing elements, found later: gallium, scandium, germanium.
textes.En 1869, Dmitri Mendeleïev range les élé: In 1869 Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the known elements in a table: in rows by increasing mass, and in columns grouping elements with similar chemical properties. Where nothing fitted, he left empty boxes and announced that unknown elements would fill them.
textes.Il les nomme d'avance : eka-aluminium, e: He named them in advance: eka-aluminium, eka-boron, eka-silicon. Gallium was discovered in 1875 by Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran, scandium in 1879, germanium in 1886: they took the predicted places. That is what made his table prevail.
textes.Liaison covalente = une paire d'électron: Covalent bond = a shared pair of electrons (Lewis, 1916). Single, double or triple depending on the number of pairs. Carbon makes 4 bonds.
textes.En 1916, Gilbert Lewis propose une idée: In 1916 Gilbert Lewis proposed a simple idea: two atoms stay bonded when they share a pair of electrons. That is the covalent bond. In H₂, each hydrogen brings one electron; the pair belongs to both at once.
textes.Deux atomes peuvent partager une, deux o: Two atoms can share one, two or three pairs: a single, double or triple bond. The two oxygens of O₂ are joined by a double bond. Carbon, with its four valence electrons, forms four bonds: that is what lets it build chains and rings.
textes.Électronégativité (Pauling, 1932) : peti: Electronegativity (Pauling, 1932): small gap = covalent, medium gap = polar, large gap (over 1.7) = ionic.
textes.Dans une liaison, les deux atomes ne tir: In a bond, the two atoms do not pull on the electrons with the same strength. Linus Pauling put a number on it in 1932: electronegativity. Fluorine is the greediest (3.98), oxygen follows (3.44), hydrogen is at 2.20, sodium at 0.93.
textes.Tout dépend de l'écart. Presque nul (jus: It all depends on the gap. Almost none (up to about 0.3): fair sharing. Between 0.3 and 1.7: the bond is polar, one side carries a little negative charge. Above 1.7 it is usually ionic: one atom simply takes the electron. Between sodium and chlorine (3.16) the gap is over 2: salt is made of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. These thresholds are guides, not sharp borders.
textes.L'eau est polaire et coudée ; ses liaiso: Water is polar and bent; its hydrogen bonds explain its boiling at 100 °C and floating ice.
textes.Ces accroches expliquent les bizarreries: These grips explain water's oddities. Hydrogen sulfide, H₂S, almost twice as heavy, is a gas at room temperature, while water only boils at 100 °C. And on freezing, hydrogen bonds arrange the molecules in an open lattice: ice (0.917 g/mL) is about 9 % less dense than liquid water. It floats, and lakes freeze from the top.
textes.Une échelle qui compte par dix: A scale that counts in tens
textes.pH = −log[H⁺] (Sørensen, 1909). Une unit: pH = −log[H⁺] (Sørensen, 1909). One unit lower = 10 times more acidic.
textes.En 1909, au laboratoire Carlsberg de Cop: In 1909, at the Carlsberg laboratory in Copenhagen, Søren Sørensen invented pH to measure acidity. Below 7 a solution is acidic; at 7, neutral; above, basic. Lemon juice is around 2, vinegar around 3, pure water 7, bleach around 12.
textes.Le piège, c'est que l'échelle est logari: The catch is that the scale is logarithmic: pH is the exponent of the H⁺ ion concentration, with its sign changed. 10⁻³ mol/L gives a pH of 3, 10⁻⁴ a pH of 4. Going down by a single unit therefore means ten times more H⁺ ions; by two units, a hundred times more.
textes.Un acide donne, une base prend: An acid gives, a base takes
textes.Acide = donneur de H⁺, base = capteur de: Acid = H⁺ donor, base = H⁺ acceptor (Brønsted and Lowry, 1923). Acid + base → salt + water.
textes.La définition la plus utile date de 1923: The most useful definition dates from 1923: the Dane Johannes Brønsted and the Englishman Martin Lowry, independently, said an acid is a species that gives up an H⁺ ion, and a base one that takes it. Before them, Svante Arrhenius, building on his 1884 work on ions in water, spoke of acids that release H⁺ in solution.
textes.Quand un acide rencontre une base en bon: When an acid meets a base in the right proportions, the H⁺ of one and the OH⁻ of the other form water, and a salt remains: that is neutralisation. That is what the bicarbonate in a heartburn remedy does: it neutralises part of the hydrochloric acid in gastric juice.
textes.Le sang ne plaisante pas avec le pH: Blood does not joke about pH
textes.Un tampon (acide faible + sa base) amort: A buffer (weak acid + its base) dampens pH changes: blood stays between 7.35 and 7.45 thanks to bicarbonate.
textes.Le sang humain se tient entre pH 7,35 et: Human blood stays between pH 7.35 and 7.45. Outside that narrow window, acidosis or alkalosis sets in quickly. What holds it there is a buffer: a weak acid and base pair, here carbonic acid and bicarbonate, which soaks up extra H⁺ or supplies it when it runs short.
textes.Les océans, eux, n'ont pas un tampon inf: The oceans do not have an infinite buffer. They absorb part of the CO₂ we emit, which forms carbonic acid: surface pH has gone from about 8.2 to 8.1 since the 19th century. Only a tenth of a unit, but on a scale that counts in tens, that is about 30 % more H⁺ ions.
textes.Rien ne se crée : on recompte les atomes: Nothing is created: count the atoms again
textes.Conservation de la masse (Lomonossov 175: Conservation of mass (Lomonosov 1756, Lavoisier 1773): as many atoms of each kind before and after.
textes.Un bois qui brûle semble perdre du poids: Burning wood seems to lose weight, rusting metal seems to gain some. Antoine Lavoisier ran reactions in sealed vessels and weighed everything: the total mass does not change. He stated it as early as 1773 and popularised the principle, which buried the phlogiston theory. The Russian Mikhail Lomonosov had stated it as early as 1756.
textes.Dans une réaction, les atomes changent d: In a reaction, atoms change partners; they are neither born nor destroyed. Hence balancing: in 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O, there are 4 hydrogens and 2 oxygens on each side. If the counts do not match, the equation is wrong.
textes.Énergie d'activation (Arrhenius, 1889) :: Activation energy (Arrhenius, 1889): the barrier to get over. Heat = more molecules get over; catalyst = lower barrier, without being used up.
textes.Une allumette ne s'enflamme pas toute se: A match does not light by itself in its box: it has to be struck. Every reaction has an energy barrier to get over, the activation energy, a term introduced by Svante Arrhenius in 1889. The hotter it is, the more molecules have enough energy to get over: that is why the fridge slows the reactions that spoil food.
textes.Un catalyseur abaisse cette barrière : l: A catalyst lowers that barrier: the reaction goes faster, and the catalyst comes out unchanged. It changes neither the starting point nor the end point, only the path. Enzymes are life's catalysts; a car's catalytic converter is another.
textes.Oxydation = perte d'électrons, réduction: Oxidation = loss of electrons, reduction = gain. A battery sends those electrons through a circuit (Volta, 1800).
textes.S'oxyder, c'est perdre des électrons ; s: To be oxidised is to lose electrons; to be reduced is to gain them. The two always go together: the electrons lost by one are taken by the other. Rusting iron is oxidised; the oxygen attacking it is reduced.
textes.Si l'on force ces électrons à passer par: If those electrons are forced through a wire, you get a current. That was Alessandro Volta's idea; he described his pile to the Royal Society on 20 March 1800: stacked zinc and copper discs, separated by cloth soaked in brine. All our batteries still work that way.
textes.Solide, liquide, gaz = mêmes molécules,: Solid, liquid, gas = same molecules, different jiggling. Sublimation = solid → gas directly.
textes.Glace, eau, vapeur : ce sont les mêmes m: Ice, water, steam: the same H₂O molecules. What changes is how much they jiggle and how far apart they are. In a solid they vibrate in place; in a liquid they slide past each other; in a gas they fly off and spread out.
textes.Pourquoi le glaçon reste à 0 °C: Why the ice cube stays at 0 °C
textes.Pendant un changement d'état, la tempéra: During a change of state, the temperature stays constant. Melting 1 g of ice ≈ heating 1 g of water by 80 °C.
textes.C'est pour cela que la glace refroidit s: That is why ice cools a drink so well: it soaks up heat without warming up. And salt on an icy road heats nothing: it lowers the temperature at which water freezes, down to about −21 °C for salt water.
textes.P × V constant à température fixe (Boyle: P × V constant at fixed temperature (Boyle 1662, Mariotte 1676); P V = n R T (Clapeyron, 1834). Lower pressure = lower boiling point.
textes.À température constante, si on divise pa: At constant temperature, halve a gas's volume and its pressure doubles: P × V stays constant. Robert Boyle published it in 1662, Edme Mariotte in 1676. Émile Clapeyron combined these laws in 1834 into a single formula, P V = n R T: pressure, volume, amount of gas and temperature are linked.
textes.Une conséquence concrète : la températur: A concrete consequence: the boiling point depends on pressure. Under one atmosphere water boils at 100 °C; at altitude the air weighs less and it boils earlier, around 70 °C at the top of Everest. Pasta cooks badly there, and the opposite happens in a pressure cooker, where pressure rises and water goes above 100 °C.
textes.Organique = chimie du carbone, qui fait: Organic = carbon chemistry; carbon makes 4 bonds. Wöhler (1828) synthesised urea, but did not kill vitalism on his own.
textes.La chimie organique, c'est la chimie des: Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds. With its four bonds, carbon links to itself in chains, branches and rings, and to hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen: hence millions of different molecules, from methane CH₄ to proteins.
textes.On a longtemps cru qu'il fallait une « f: People long believed a "vital force" was needed to make these molecules. In 1828 Friedrich Wöhler obtained urea from mineral compounds. Textbooks often make it the death blow to vitalism, but that is a simplified legend: Wöhler was not on a crusade, and other syntheses, such as Kolbe's acetic acid in 1845, counted just as much.
textes.Benzène : isolé par Faraday (1825), anne: Benzene: isolated by Faraday (1825), 6-carbon ring proposed by Kekulé (1865). The snake dream was told in 1890.
textes.Le benzène, isolé par Michael Faraday en: Benzene, isolated by Michael Faraday in 1825, was long a puzzle: six carbons, six hydrogens, and yet surprisingly stable. In 1865 August Kekulé proposed a ring of six carbons, with alternating single and double bonds.
textes.En 1890, pour les 25 ans de sa découvert: In 1890, for the 25th anniversary of his discovery, Kekulé told how the idea came to him while daydreaming by the fire: a snake biting its own tail. A nice story, told a quarter of a century later; nobody knows how far to believe it. The ring stayed: it is found in aspirin, paracetamol and polystyrene.
textes.Polymère = longue chaîne d'un motif répé: Polymer = long chain of a repeated unit (plastics, cellulose, DNA). Staudinger (1920, Nobel 1953) made the case against general opinion.
textes.Un polymère est une molécule immense fai: A polymer is a huge molecule made of a unit repeated thousands of times. The polyethylene of bags is a chain of –CH₂–CH₂–. Nature is full of them: wood's cellulose, starch, proteins, DNA.
textes.En 1920, Hermann Staudinger affirme que: In 1920 Hermann Staudinger claimed that rubber or cellulose were real long chains held by covalent bonds. The big names of the day, such as Emil Fischer, did not believe it: to them these were clumps of small molecules. Staudinger held firm and received the Nobel Prize in 1953. Meanwhile Bakelite (1907) and nylon (1935) had launched the plastic age.
textes.Savon = graisse + soude (saponification): Soap = fat + lye (saponification). A head that likes water, a tail that likes grease: micelles carry the dirt away.
textes.Le savon se fabrique en mélangeant des g: Soap is made by mixing fats or oils with a strong base, lye: the fats split into fatty acid salts, and glycerol is left over. That is saponification. Traces of soap-like materials go back to about 2800 BCE, in Babylon.
textes.Chaque molécule de savon a une tête qui: Each soap molecule has a head that likes water and a tail that likes grease. In water the tails dive into the grease while the heads stay on the outside: they form little balls, micelles, that trap the dirt. Rinsing carries them away.
textes.Maillard (1912) : sucres + acides aminés: Maillard (1912): sugars + amino acids + heat (140 to 165 °C) = browning and aromas. No crust in boiling water.
textes.La croûte du pain, la viande grillée, le: Bread crust, grilled meat, roasted coffee: that is the Maillard reaction, described in 1912 by the French chemist Louis Camille Maillard. Sugars and amino acids react with heat and produce hundreds of brown, fragrant molecules.
textes.Elle va vite autour de 140 à 165 °C. Voi: It goes fast at around 140 to 165 °C. That is why boiled meat does not brown: in water you cannot go above 100 °C. To sear, you need a hot pan and a dry surface.
textes.Du saule à l'aspirine, et ce qu'il ne fa: From willow to aspirin, and what not to mix
Aspirin comes from willow (Bayer, 1899). Bleach + acid = toxic chlorine: never mix household products.
textes.Les plantes riches en salicylés, comme l: Salicylate-rich plants such as willow already appear on Sumerian tablets and in the Egyptian Ebers papyrus; around 400 BCE Hippocrates described a tea against fever. In 1897, at Bayer, chemists looked for a version gentler on the stomach, and by 1899 acetylsalicylic acid was sold worldwide under the name Aspirin.
textes.La chimie de la maison a aussi ses dange: Household chemistry has its dangers too. Bleach mixed with an acid, such as a descaler or vinegar, releases chlorine gas, which is toxic. Simple rule: never mix two household products.
textes.Une plaque voilée dans un tiroir: A fogged plate in a drawer
textes.Becquerel (1896), les Curie (1898). Alph: Becquerel (1896), the Curies (1898). Alpha: paper; beta: aluminium; gamma: lead or concrete.
textes.En 1896, Henri Becquerel range des sels: In 1896 Henri Becquerel put uranium salts on a photographic plate in a drawer, for lack of sunshine for his experiment. The plate was fogged anyway: uranium gives off radiation on its own. In 1898 Marie and Pierre Curie discovered two far more active elements, polonium and radium.
textes.En 1899, Ernest Rutherford trie ces rayo: In 1899 Ernest Rutherford sorted these rays by what stops them: he called alpha those stopped by a few thin sheets, beta those that get through. Gamma came later. Alpha particles, helium nuclei, stop on a sheet of paper; beta on a few millimetres of aluminium; gamma rays, a very energetic light, need lead or thick concrete.
textes.La moitié, puis la moitié de la moitié: Half, then half of the half
textes.Demi-vie : la moitié se désintègre, quel: Half-life: half decays, whatever the amount. Carbon-14: 5,730 years, dating back to about 50,000 years (Libby).
textes.On ne peut pas prévoir quand un noyau ra: Nobody can predict when a radioactive nucleus will decay, but we know how long it takes for half of a batch to do so: the half-life. It does not depend on the amount. After one half-life half remains, after two a quarter, after three an eighth: never zero all at once.
textes.Le carbone 14 en fait une horloge. Il na: Carbon-14 turns this into a clock. It is born high in the atmosphere, when neutrons produced by cosmic rays strike nitrogen. Living things take it in while they live, then the stock runs down with a half-life of about 5,730 years. Willard Libby developed the method in Chicago in the late 1940s (Nobel Prize 1960); it reaches back about 50,000 years.
textes.Fission (Hahn et Strassmann 1938, Meitne: Fission (Hahn and Strassmann 1938, Meitner and Frisch 1939): a heavy nucleus splits, chain reaction (Chicago, 1942). Fusion: light nuclei join (the Sun).
textes.En décembre 1938, Otto Hahn et Fritz Str: In December 1938, Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann found barium after bombarding uranium with neutrons: the nucleus had split in two. In early 1939 Lise Meitner and her nephew Otto Frisch explained it, and Frisch called it fission, like the division of cells. Each fission releases about 200 MeV and neutrons that can trigger others: a chain reaction.
textes.Le 2 décembre 1942, sous les gradins du: On 2 December 1942, under the stands of Stagg Field at the University of Chicago, on a former squash court, Enrico Fermi's pile, uranium in 45,000 graphite blocks, sustained the first controlled chain reaction, at about half a watt. The Sun does the opposite: it fuses hydrogen nuclei into helium.
textes.Ce qui fait qu'un atome est du carbone p: What makes an atom carbon rather than nitrogen is its number of protons: the atomic number. Carbon has 6, oxygen 8, iron 26. Change that number and you change the element. It was the young English physicist Henry Moseley who showed it in 1913, by measuring the X-rays of the elements: the atomic number is the charge of the nucleus, and it put the table in order. He was killed two years later at Gallipoli, on 10 August 1915, aged 27.

textes.L'échelle du pH est logarithmique. Les l: The pH scale is logarithmic. Logarithms were published in 1614 by the Scot John Napier; Laplace would say they "doubled the life of the astronomer" by shortening their calculations.
textes.L'acide citrique est isolé du jus de cit: Citric acid was isolated from lemon juice in 1784 by the Swede Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Today it is mostly made by fermentation with a mould, Aspergillus niger.
textes.La première définition moderne des acide: The first modern definition of acids and bases came from Svante Arrhenius, in the 1880s: an acid releases H⁺ in water, a base OH⁻. When they meet, they make water.
textes.Brønsted et Lowry proposent cette défini: Brønsted and Lowry proposed this definition independently, in 1923. The same year, Gilbert Lewis published another theory, based on electron pairs.

textes.Les plus anciennes traces de fabrication: The oldest traces of vinegar-making go back to the Babylonians, around 3000 BC. Much later, Louis Pasteur identified the bacteria that do the work.
textes.L'eau de Javel doit son nom au village d: Bleach (eau de Javel) is named after the village of Javel, near Paris, where Claude-Louis Berthollet made the first in 1789. Antoine Labarraque later made it cheaper with soda.

textes.Depuis 1850, le pH moyen de surface des: Since 1850, the average surface pH of the oceans has gone from about 8.17 to 8.08 in 2021. The ocean absorbs about a quarter of the CO₂ we emit.

textes.La première équation chimique dessinée e: The first diagrammed chemical equation is credited to the Frenchman Jean Beguin, in 1615.
textes.Le mot « catalyse » est forgé par Berzel: The word "catalysis" was coined by Berzelius in 1835. But the Scot Elizabeth Fulhame had described the phenomenon as early as 1794, in a book on oxidation and reduction.
textes.Le mot « oxygène » a été choisi par Lavo: The word "oxygen" was chosen by Lavoisier in 1777. He was the first to understand its role in combustion.
textes.Aristote note déjà que les braises dégag: Aristotle already noted that burning coals give off toxic fumes. In 1857, Claude Bernard showed that carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin and stops blood from carrying oxygen.
textes.Le gaz de ces bulles est l'« air fixe »: The gas in these bubbles is Joseph Black's "fixed air": he got it from limestone attacked by an acid, just as baking soda is attacked by vinegar here.
textes.En 1889, Svante Arrhenius relie la vites: In 1889, Svante Arrhenius linked reaction speed to an "activation energy" that molecules must overcome. The colder it is, the fewer manage it.
textes.Fermier général, Lavoisier est guillotin: A tax farmer, Lavoisier was guillotined on 8 May 1794. Lagrange: "It took them only an instant to cut off this head, and a hundred years might not suffice to reproduce its like."
textes.Le 20 mars 1800, Alessandro Volta décrit: On 20 March 1800, Alessandro Volta described to the Royal Society his pile of copper and zinc discs separated by cardboard soaked in salt water. He had been inspired by Luigi Galvani's frog legs.
textes.La glace carbonique est observée pour la: Dry ice was first observed in 1835 by the Frenchman Adrien-Jean-Pierre Thilorier. The English name "dry ice" was trademarked in 1925.
textes.L'échelle d'Anders Celsius, en 1742, éta: Anders Celsius's 1742 scale was upside down: 0 for boiling water, 100 for ice. Linnaeus flipped it in 1745, a year after his death.
textes.En 1761, l'Écossais Joseph Black compren: In 1761, the Scot Joseph Black realised that heat given to melting ice goes into changing its state, not raising its temperature: "latent heat".
textes.Boyle doit sa loi à une pompe à vide per: Boyle owed his law to a vacuum pump improved with Robert Hooke's help. Henry Power had formulated the hypothesis in 1661, and Boyle cited it in 1662, mistakenly crediting Richard Towneley.
textes.Le mot « plasma » est introduit en 1928: The word "plasma" was introduced in 1928 by American chemist Irving Langmuir, probably by analogy with blood plasma, which carries particles.
textes.L'azote est liquéfié pour la première fo: Nitrogen was first liquefied on 15 April 1883 at the Jagiellonian University in Kraków, by Polish physicists Zygmunt Wróblewski and Karol Olszewski.
textes.Van Helmont emploie le mot « gaz » dans: Van Helmont used the word "gas" in his 1652 Ortus medicinae. He wrote that he had chosen it as "not far from chaos", the Greek word.
textes.Berzelius est le premier à distinguer le: Berzelius was the first to distinguish organic compounds, which contain carbon, from inorganic ones. He also gave us the words "protein" (1838) and "polymer" (1833).
textes.Les historiens nuancent ce récit : Wöhle: Historians qualify this story: Wöhler was no crusader against the vital force, and the idea was already in retreat. A 2000 survey found this "Wöhler myth" in 90% of chemistry textbooks.
textes.En 1920, Hermann Staudinger propose que: In 1920, Hermann Staudinger proposed that rubber, starch and proteins are very long chains. Almost all his colleagues rejected the idea; he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1953.
textes.En 1897, Eduard Buchner fait fermenter d: In 1897, Eduard Buchner fermented sugar with mere juice from crushed yeast, without living cells: fermentation is due to enzymes. Nobel Prize 1907.
textes.En 1797, Smithson Tennant brûle diamant: In 1797, Smithson Tennant burned diamond and graphite and obtained the same amount of gas: they are two forms of the same element.
textes.Wallace Carothers se suicide en avril 19: Wallace Carothers took his own life in April 1937, sixteen months before nylon was publicly announced. He never saw his invention go on sale.
textes.Kekulé dit en 1890 que l'idée du cycle d: In 1890 Kekulé said the idea of the benzene ring came to him in a daydream of a snake biting its own tail. Some historians suspect the story was made up.
textes.Avant la bakélite, le Belge Leo Baekelan: Before Bakelite, the Belgian Leo Baekeland had made his fortune with Velox, the first commercially successful photographic paper: his company was bought in 1899 by George Eastman of Kodak for $750,000.
textes.Une étude de la NOAA prédit dès 1988 une: A NOAA paper predicted as early as 1988 a zone where plastic would accumulate in the North Pacific. Sailor Charles Moore crossed it in 1997 and made it known.
textes.Le 27 août 1859, près de Titusville en P: On 27 August 1859, near Titusville, Pennsylvania, Edwin Drake's well struck oil at 21 metres: the first commercial oil well in the United States.
textes.Louis Camille Maillard décrit en 1912 la: Louis Camille Maillard described the reaction between sugars and amino acids in 1912. He died in Paris in 1936.
textes.Les plus anciennes traces de fabrication: The oldest traces of soap-like materials come from Babylon, around 2800 BC. Pliny the Elder credited soap to the Gauls.
textes.Le chlore est étudié en 1774 par Scheele: Chlorine was studied in 1774 by Scheele, and Humphry Davy named it in 1810 from the Greek for "pale green". It was used as a chemical weapon from 1915, in the First World War.
textes.Des tablettes sumériennes et le papyrus: Sumerian tablets and the Ebers papyrus already mention willow. In 1897, at Bayer, Felix Hoffmann (or perhaps Arthur Eichengrün) obtained pure acetylsalicylic acid; the name Aspirin dates from 1899.
textes.La première pile, celle de Volta, est dé: The first battery, Volta's, was described in 1800. It came out of a dispute: Luigi Galvani thought the frog produced the electricity, Volta that it came from the two metals.
textes.Le PTFE découvert par Roy Plunkett en 19: The PTFE discovered by Roy Plunkett in 1938 took the trade name Teflon in 1945. Heat-resistant and inert, it is also used to insulate cables and coat medical implants.
textes.Le ciment Portland est breveté par l'Ang: Portland cement was patented by the Englishman Joseph Aspdin in 1824, and reinforced concrete invented by Joseph Monier in 1849. The Romans already used concrete widely: the Pantheon's dome is the largest in unreinforced concrete.
textes.Les feux d'artifice sont nés en Chine, s: Fireworks were born in China, under the Song dynasty (960-1279). Modern bright colours come from chlorate chemistry: in 1786, Berthollet observed the violet flame of potassium chlorate.
textes.Becquerel avait rangé ses plaques et ses: Becquerel had stored his plates and uranium salts in a drawer on 26 and 27 February 1896, for lack of sun. On 1 March, the plates were fogged anyway. He shared the 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie.
textes.La notion de demi-vie vient d'Ernest Rut: The idea of half-life comes from Ernest Rutherford, in 1907, who used it to date rocks. The term "half-life" took hold in the early 1950s.
textes.La datation au carbone 14 est mise au po: Carbon-14 dating was developed in 1949 by Willard Libby at the University of Chicago, tested on sequoias of known age from their rings. Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1960.
textes.Le mot « isotope », « même place » en gr: The word "isotope", Greek for "same place", was suggested to Frederick Soddy in 1913 by the physician Margaret Todd. Why isotopes differ was only understood in 1932, with the neutron.
textes.Lise Meitner, qui avait dû fuir l'Allema: Lise Meitner, who had had to flee Nazi Germany in July 1938, explained fission with her nephew Otto Frisch at Christmas 1938. The 1944 Nobel went to Otto Hahn alone; element 109 now bears her name, meitnerium.
textes.En 1938-1939, Hans Bethe explique commen: In 1938-1939, Hans Bethe explained how stars shine through fusion reactions, first for the Sun with Charles Critchfield. Nobel Prize in Physics 1967.
textes.Marie Curie est la première femme à rece: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel, and one of only two people awarded in two fields, with Linus Pauling. Her notebooks, still radioactive, are kept in lead-lined boxes.
textes.Le becquerel est adopté comme unité offi: The becquerel was adopted as an official unit in 1975, replacing the curie, a unit based on the activity of one gram of radium.
textes.C'est Rutherford qui, en 1899, distingue: It was Rutherford who, in 1899, distinguished alpha and beta rays by their penetrating power. In 1909, with Thomas Royds, he showed that alpha particles are helium nuclei.
textes.Il faut près de deux ans à Grace Fryer e: It took Grace Fryer and four colleagues about two years to find a lawyer. The case opened in January 1928 and settled that autumn: $10,000 each and a lifetime annuity.
textes.Ce jour-là, Arthur Compton prévient Jame: That day, Arthur Compton told James Conant in code: "The Italian navigator has landed in the New World." Eugene Wigner brought out a bottle of Chianti, drunk from paper cups.
textes.{comp}. Paracelse a brûlé en public le C: {comp}. Paracelsus publicly burned Avicenna's Canon. Just burn your doubts.
textes.Chimie. Lavoisier pesait tout, même l'ai: Chemistry. Lavoisier weighed everything, even air. I weigh your answers. {comp}.
textes.Newton cherchait la pierre philosophale: Newton secretly searched for the philosopher's stone. I'm searching for your weak spot: {comp}.
textes.Juste. Rien ne se perd, rien ne se crée: Right. Nothing is lost, nothing is created: your points turn into progress. Lavoisier approves.
textes.Bonne réponse. Mendeleïev laissait des c: Good answer. Mendeleev left empty squares. You've just filled one.
textes.Correct. Marie Curie gardait des tubes d: Correct. Marie Curie kept tubes of radium in her pocket. You keep a cool head.
textes.Réaction réussie. Pas d'explosion. Je su: Reaction successful. No explosion. I'm almost disappointed.
textes.Raté. Les alchimistes ont cherché l'or p: Missed. Alchemists looked for gold for centuries. You've been looking for the right answer for ten seconds. Patience.
textes.Faux. Le phlogistique a régné un siècle: Wrong. Phlogiston reigned for a century before Lavoisier drove it out. Your error will last less long.
textes.Erreur. Hennig Brand cherchait de l'or d: Error. Hennig Brand looked for gold in urine and found phosphorus. You found nothing at all.
textes.Précipité au fond du tube. Votre score,: Precipitated to the bottom of the tube. Your score, I mean.
textes.En 1869, il range les éléments dans un t: In 1869, he arranged the elements in a table and left empty squares in it for elements not yet known, whose properties he predicted. Gallium and germanium arrived a few years later. He only cut his hair once a year.
textes.Né esclave dans le Missouri, il devient: Born a slave in Missouri, he became a botanist and chemist at the Tuskegee Institute. He taught farmers to alternate cotton, which exhausts the soil, with peanuts, which enrich it with nitrogen, and looked for hundreds of uses for these plants. Contrary to legend, he did not invent peanut butter.
textes.Physicienne autrichienne, elle fuit l'Al: An Austrian physicist, she fled Nazi Germany in 1938. A few months later, with her nephew Otto Frisch, she explained the results of her former colleague Otto Hahn: the uranium nucleus had split in two, it was fission. The Nobel went to Hahn alone. Element 109 bears her name.
textes.Biologiste marine, elle publie en 1962 P: A marine biologist, in 1962 she published Silent Spring, about the damage done by pesticides like DDT. The chemical industry called her a “fanatic.” A presidential science committee largely backed her in 1963, and agricultural DDT was banned in the United States in 1972. She died of cancer two years after the book.
textes.Il invente l'électronégativité en 1932 e: He invented electronegativity in 1932 and published The Nature of the Chemical Bond in 1939. Two unshared Nobel Prizes, chemistry and peace. He also got things spectacularly wrong: he proposed a triple helix for DNA, and believed high doses of vitamin C prevented colds.
textes.Sa thèse de 1884 sur les ions en solutio: His 1884 thesis on ions in solution, which defined acids and bases, received the lowest grade that still allowed it to pass. It earned him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1903. In 1896, he also calculated that doubling the CO₂ in the air would warm the Earth by several degrees.
textes.En 1908 à Leyde, il liquéfie l'hélium à: In 1908 in Leiden, he liquefied helium at four degrees above absolute zero. Three years later, he discovered that mercury, just as cold, loses all electrical resistance: superconductivity. His laboratory's motto: “Door meten tot weten,” through measurement to knowledge.
textes.Maîtriser les acides et les bases. Votre: Master acids and bases. Your tongue was already detecting them everywhere.
textes.La « carte de la langue » (le sucré au b: The “tongue map” (sweet at the tip, bitter at the back) is wrong: every area perceives every taste. It comes from a loose reading, in 1942, of a 1901 German thesis that only described small differences in sensitivity.
textes.Maîtriser les liaisons chimiques. Les vi: Master chemical bonds. The stained glass of Chartres can rest easy.
textes.Les vitraux anciens sont parfois plus ép: Old stained-glass windows are sometimes thicker at the bottom, but not because the glass “flows”: glaziers often put the thick side at the bottom. A 1998 calculation shows it would take far longer than the age of the Universe for a window to visibly deform.
textes.Maîtriser les atomes et les éléments. Sa: Master atoms and elements. Without sleeping on it, if possible.
textes.Mendeleïev aurait raconté avoir vu son t: Mendeleev supposedly said he saw his table in a dream. Historians mostly point out that he had been working for years to sort his element cards, like a game of solitaire.
textes.Maîtriser les réactions chimiques. Votre: Master chemical reactions. Your XP, on the other hand, can be lost.
textes.Car rien ne se crée, ni dans les opérati: For nothing is created, either in the operations of art or in those of nature.
Master the first diamond of Alchemy.
textes.Newton n'a pas été le premier de l'âge d: Newton was not the first of the age of reason. He was the last of the magicians.
textes.Maîtriser 3 compétences. L'arbre de la C: Master 3 skills. The tree of Chemistry opens.
textes.« Rien ne se perd, rien ne se crée, tout: “Nothing is lost, nothing is created, everything is transformed” is not Lavoisier's word for word. In 1789 he wrote that “nothing is created, either in the operations of art or in those of nature.” The snappy formula came after him.
textes.Maîtriser les états de la matière. L'eau: Master the states of matter. Water boils sooner in the mountains. Your pasta knows it too.
textes.En 1835, dans les Andes, Darwin et ses g: In 1835, in the Andes, Darwin and his guides boiled potatoes all night: in the morning, they were still hard. At altitude, the pressure drops and water boils before 100 °C. At the top of Everest, around 70 °C.
textes.Maîtriser la chimie organique. La « forc: Master organic chemistry. The “vital force” took decades to die.
textes.On raconte qu'en 1828, en fabriquant de: The story goes that in 1828, by making urea in the laboratory, Friedrich Wöhler killed off at a stroke the idea that a “vital force” is needed to produce the molecules of life. The chemists of the time hardly saw it that way. The heroic account was written after the fact, in textbooks.
textes.Maîtriser la chimie du quotidien. Le glu: Master everyday chemistry. Glutamate is in tomatoes and Parmesan too.
textes.En 1968, une lettre au New England Journ: In 1968, a letter to the New England Journal of Medicine described palpitations after a Chinese meal and suspected glutamate. The idea went around the world. Double-blind trials find no effect at food doses. Glutamate is naturally present in tomatoes and Parmesan.
Master radioactivity and the nucleus. Don't drink anything that glows.
textes.Dans les années 1920, on vend du Raditho: In the 1920s, Radithor was sold, a radium water supposed to restore vigor. The industrialist Eben Byers drank about 1,400 bottles. He died in 1932, his jaw eaten away. In 1990, the Wall Street Journal summed it up: “The Radium Water Worked Fine Until His Jaw Came Off.”
textes.Réussir trois quiz d'Alchimie sans faute: Pass three Alchemy quizzes without a mistake. No gold, but a light.
textes.En 1669, à Hambourg, l'alchimiste Hennig: In 1669, in Hamburg, the alchemist Hennig Brand looked for the philosopher's stone by boiling urine, lots of urine. He got no gold, but a substance that glowed in the dark: phosphorus, the first element whose discoverer we know.
textes.le Soleil, qui en brûle 600 millions de: the Sun, which burns 600 million tonnes of it per second
textes.C'est l'élément le plus abondant de l'Un: It is the most abundant element in the Universe: about three quarters of visible matter. Cavendish called it “inflammable air.”
textes.Découvert dans le spectre du Soleil en 1: Discovered in the Sun's spectrum in 1868, before being found on Earth. Hence its name, after Helios.
textes.Il est si léger qu'il flotte sur l'huile: It is so light that it floats on oil. It cannot be stored under oil like sodium: it is coated in petroleum jelly.
textes.les miroirs du télescope James Webb: the mirrors of the James Webb telescope
textes.Les miroirs du télescope James Webb sont: The James Webb telescope's mirrors are made of gold-coated beryllium: light, stiff and stable in deep cold.
textes.Le verre borosilicaté supporte les chocs: Borosilicate glass withstands thermal shock: that is why you can take a Pyrex dish from the oven to the countertop.
textes.Graphite et diamant sont faits du même a: Graphite and diamond are made of the same atom, arranged differently. One crumbles on paper, the other scratches glass.
textes.l'air qu'on respire, aux quatre cinquièm: the air we breathe, four fifths of it
textes.Une souris n'y survit pas, avaient noté: A mouse cannot survive in it, Priestley and Cavendish noted; Lavoisier named it “azote,” “lifeless.” Yet it makes up 78% of the air.
textes.C'est l'élément le plus abondant de la c: It is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust by mass: almost half.
textes.Si réactif qu'il a blessé ou tué plusieu: So reactive that it injured or killed several chemists. Moissan finally isolated it in 1886 and won the Nobel Prize in 1906.
Only pure neon glows red-orange. The other colors of “neon” lights come from other gases or powders.
textes.Jeté dans l'eau, il file, fond et peut e: Thrown into water, it darts around, melts and can explode. Davy isolated it in 1807 with an electric battery.
textes.Au cœur de chaque molécule de chlorophyl: At the heart of every chlorophyll molecule is a magnesium atom.
textes.Au XIXe siècle, il valait plus cher que: In the 19th century, it was worth more than gold. Napoleon III kept his aluminum cutlery for his most distinguished guests.
textes.Deuxième élément de la croûte terrestre,: Second element of the Earth's crust, after oxygen. Beach sand is mostly silica.
textes.Brand l'a découvert en 1669 en faisant b: Brand discovered it in 1669 by boiling buckets of urine. He was looking for the philosopher's stone.
textes.La Bible fait pleuvoir du soufre ardent: The Bible rains burning brimstone on Sodom and Gomorrah. The rotten egg smell is hydrogen sulfide.
textes.Gaz vert et toxique, il a servi d'arme à: A green, toxic gas, it was used as a weapon at Ypres in 1915. It also disinfects the drinking water of billions of people.
textes.Son nom vient du grec « paresseux » : il: Its name comes from the Greek for “lazy”: it reacts with almost nothing. Yet it makes up nearly 1% of the air.
textes.Son symbole K vient du latin kalium. Dav: Its symbol K comes from the Latin kalium. Davy isolated it in 1807, a few days before sodium.
textes.Le corps humain en contient environ un k: The human body contains about a kilogram of it, almost all in the skeleton.
textes.Une des cases vides de Mendeleïev, qu'il: One of Mendeleev's empty squares, which he called “eka-boron.” Nilson discovered it in 1879.
textes.L'essentiel du titane extrait finit en b: Most of the titanium mined ends up as titanium white, a very opaque pigment: paint, paper, sunscreen.
textes.Henry Ford utilisait de l'acier au vanad: Henry Ford used vanadium steel in the Model T, lighter and stronger.
textes.Son nom vient du grec « couleur » : ses: Its name comes from the Greek for “color”: its compounds are green, yellow, orange. The ruby owes it its red.
textes.Les artistes de la préhistoire ont peint: Prehistoric artists painted caves with manganese black, tens of thousands of years ago.
textes.Le noyau terrestre est surtout fait de f: The Earth's core is mostly iron. Beyond iron, fusion no longer yields energy: when the core of a big star is full of it, the star collapses.
textes.Les mineurs allemands accusaient le kobo: German miners blamed the kobold, a goblin, for spoiling their ore. Cobalt kept the name.
textes.Encore un lutin : Kupfernickel, « le cui: Another goblin: Kupfernickel, “the devil's copper,” the ore that looked like copper without yielding any.
textes.La statue de la Liberté était couleur cu: The Statue of Liberty was copper-colored when it arrived. Verdigris covered it in about twenty years.
textes.Les toits gris de Paris sont en zinc, po: The gray rooftops of Paris are zinc, laid en masse during Haussmann's works.
textes.la cuillère qui fond dans le thé: the spoon that melts in tea
textes.Il fond à 30 °C, donc dans la main. Mend: It melts at 30 °C, so in your hand. Mendeleev had predicted its mass and density under the name eka-aluminum.
textes.Encore une prédiction de Mendeleïev, l'é: Another of Mendeleev's predictions, eka-silicon. Winkler found it in 1886 and named it after Germany.
textes.La « poudre de succession » des empoison: Poisoners' “inheritance powder.” The Marsh test, in 1836, made it possible to detect it in corpses.
textes.Une ou deux noix du Brésil suffisent à c: One or two Brazil nuts are enough to cover the daily need for selenium. A handful is too much.
textes.Un des deux seuls éléments liquides à te: One of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature, with mercury. Its name means “stench.”
textes.De 1960 à 1983, le mètre était défini pa: From 1960 to 1983, the meter was defined by an orange line of krypton-86.
textes.les horloges atomiques des satellites GP: the atomic clocks of GPS satellites
textes.Il s'enflamme spontanément à l'air. Les: It ignites spontaneously in air. Rubidium clocks keep time aboard GPS satellites.
textes.Nommé d'après Strontian, un village écos: Named after Strontian, a Scottish village. The red in fireworks is strontium.
textes.Ytterby, une carrière suédoise, a donné: Ytterby, a Swedish quarry, gave its name to four elements: yttrium, ytterbium, terbium and erbium.
textes.La zircone cubique brille plus que le di: Cubic zirconia sparkles more than diamond, but it is less hard and weighs almost twice as much for the same size.
textes.Les aimants supraconducteurs du LHC et d: The superconducting magnets of the LHC and of MRI scanners are wound with niobium-titanium wire.
textes.Les bactéries qui fixent l'azote de l'ai: The bacteria that fix nitrogen from the air need a molybdenum enzyme.
textes.Le premier élément fabriqué par l'humain: The first element made by humans, in 1937. Its name comes from the Greek for “artificial.”
textes.Nommé d'après la Ruthénie, nom latin de: Named after Ruthenia, a Latin name for Russia, by Karl Klaus in 1844.
textes.le reflet des bijoux en or blanc: the shine of white gold jewelry
textes.En 1979, le Guinness des records offre à: In 1979, Guinness World Records gave Paul McCartney a rhodium-plated disc, rarer than platinum.
textes.les pots catalytiques des voitures essen: the catalytic converters of gasoline cars
textes.Il absorbe plus de 900 fois son volume d: It absorbs more than 900 times its volume of hydrogen, like a sponge.
textes.Meilleur conducteur de l'électricité de: The best conductor of electricity of all metals, ahead of copper. Its symbol comes from the Latin argentum.
textes.Au Japon, la maladie itai-itai, « aïe-aï: In Japan, itai-itai disease, “ouch-ouch,” was caused by cadmium released by mines.
textes.Une fine couche d'oxyde d'indium-étain,: A thin layer of indium tin oxide, transparent and conductive, lets the screen feel your finger.
textes.les soldats de plomb, qui sont souvent e: toy soldiers, which are often made of tin
textes.Plié, il « crie » : un craquement dû au: Bend it and it “cries”: a crackling caused by the crystals rubbing. Its symbol comes from the Latin stannum.
textes.Ajouté au plomb des caractères d'imprime: Added to the lead of printing type, it limits the metal's shrinkage as it cools: the letters come out sharp.
textes.les modules thermoélectriques des glaciè: the thermoelectric modules of cooler boxes
textes.Un demi-microgramme suffit à donner une: Half a microgram is enough to give garlic breath for about thirty hours. Its name comes from Tellus, the Earth.
textes.Courtois le découvre en 1811 en brûlant: Courtois discovered it in 1811 by burning seaweed to make gunpowder. A purple vapor escaped from it.
textes.les moteurs ioniques des sondes: the ion engines of space probes
textes.Gaz « noble », mais pas si noble : Bartl: A “noble” gas, but not that noble: Bartlett got it to form a compound in 1962, to general surprise.
textes.Depuis 1967, une seconde, c'est 9 192 63: Since 1967, one second has been 9,192,631,770 oscillations of the cesium-133 atom.
textes.Avant une radio de l'estomac, on boit un: Before a stomach X-ray, you drink a barium sulfate slurry, opaque to X-rays.
textes.Son nom veut dire « caché » : il s'était: Its name means “hidden”: it lay concealed in a cerium oxide until 1839.
textes.Frotté, le ferrocérium projette une gerb: Struck, ferrocerium throws out a shower of sparks: it is the lighter's flint.
textes.Les lunettes au didyme des souffleurs de: The didymium glasses of glassblowers filter out the yellow light of sodium. Didymium hid two elements.
textes.les aimants du frigo trop puissants: fridge magnets that are too strong
textes.Les aimants néodyme-fer-bore sont les pl: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are the strongest sold commercially. They pinch fingers.
textes.les piles atomiques des stimulateurs car: the atomic batteries of old pacemakers
The only lanthanide with no stable isotope. Named after Prometheus, who stole fire from the gods.
textes.Premier élément nommé d'après une person: The first element named after a person, indirectly: the mineral samarskite, after the Russian colonel Samarsky.
textes.Sous lumière ultraviolette, les billets: Under ultraviolet light, euro banknotes glow. Europium is one of the phosphors.
textes.Nommé en l'honneur du chimiste finlandai: Named in honor of the Finnish chemist Johan Gadolin, via the mineral gadolinite.
textes.Le Terfenol-D, alliage au terbium, se dé: Terfenol-D, a terbium alloy, changes shape in a magnetic field: it can make a table vibrate like a speaker.
textes.Son nom veut dire « difficile à obtenir: Its name means “hard to get.” Lecoq de Boisbaudran made more than thirty precipitations to isolate it.
textes.les pôles des aimants les plus forts: the pole pieces of the strongest magnets
textes.Nommé d'après Holmia, Stockholm en latin: Named after Holmia, Latin for Stockholm. It has the highest magnetic moment of all elements.
textes.les fibres optiques d'Internet: the optical fibers of the Internet
textes.Les amplificateurs à fibre dopée à l'erb: Erbium-doped fiber amplifiers boost Internet signals under the oceans.
textes.Nommé d'après Thulé, l'île mythique du g: Named after Thule, the mythical island of the far North. It is one of the least abundant rare earths.
textes.Quatrième élément nommé d'après le villa: The fourth element named after the village of Ytterby. Swedes are proud of their quarry.
textes.Nommé d'après Lutèce, le nom latin de Pa: Named after Lutetia, the Latin name of Paris, by Georges Urbain in 1907.
textes.Nommé d'après Hafnia, Copenhague en lati: Named after Hafnia, Latin for Copenhagen. It was hiding in zirconium, its near twin.
textes.Comme Tantale aux Enfers, il plonge dans: Like Tantalus in the Underworld, it plunges into acid without ever absorbing any: it resists almost all of them.
textes.Son symbole W vient de wolfram, « l'écum: Its symbol W comes from wolfram, “wolf's froth”: the ore devoured the smelters' tin.
textes.Le dernier élément stable découvert, en: The last stable element discovered, in 1925, by Ida Tacke, Walter Noddack and Otto Berg. Named after the Rhine.
textes.les pointes de stylos plume anciens: the tips of old fountain pens

textes.Selon Hérodote, Thalès de Milet aurait p: According to Herodotus, Thales of Miletus predicted the solar eclipse that interrupted a battle between Lydians and Medes on May 28, 585 BC. textes.Ératosthène, bibliothécaire d'Alexandrie: Eratosthenes, librarian of Alexandria, knew that in Syene, at noon on the solstice, the Sun lit the bottom of wells. The same day, in Alexandria, a stick cast a shadow of 7.2 degrees, one fiftieth of a circle. From this he deduced the Earth's circumference: about 250,000 stadia, close to the real 40,000 km depending on the length of stadion one uses. All with a stick and the rule of three.

Comparing his measurements with those of his predecessors, he discovered the precession of the equinoxes, a slow wobble of the Earth's axis that completes a circle in about 26,000 years. He discovered the mountains of the Moon, the four large moons of Jupiter, thousands of stars invisible to the naked eye, then the phases of Venus. In the Sidereus Nuncius (1610), he named Jupiter's moons the “Medicean stars,” to please the Medici.

textes.Johannes Kepler, avec les mesures de Tyc: Johannes Kepler, using Tycho Brahe's measurements, showed that Mars does not move in a circle but on an ellipse with the Sun at one focus (Astronomia nova, 1609), then extended the rule to all the planets. It took him years of calculations on the orbit of Mars, his “war with Mars.” He also earned his living writing horoscopes.

textes.En 1632, Galilée publie le Dialogue sur: In 1632, Galileo published the Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems, in which the defender of the motionless Earth is called Simplicio. Pope Urban VIII recognized his own argument, put in Simplicio's mouth, and took it as a personal insult. In 1633, the Inquisition forced Galileo to recant and sentenced him to prison, commuted to house arrest until his death. The famous “Eppur si muove” (“And yet it moves”) only appears in texts in 1757.
