textes.Bacon parle d'« instances de la croix »,: Bacon speaks of “instances of the fingerpost” (instantiae crucis), like signposts at crossroads (Novum Organum, 1620). Duhem would doubt it really exists in physics.
textes.Selon Hérodote, Thalès aurait prédit une: According to Herodotus, Thales predicted a solar eclipse that halted a battle between Lydians and Medes, probably the one of 28 May 585 BC; some historians doubt it. Plato also tells how he fell into a well while gazing at the stars, mocked by a servant girl.
textes.Socrate dit avoir commencé à interroger: Socrates said he began questioning people after his friend Chaerephon consulted the Oracle of Delphi. Plato staged this method in his early dialogues, such as the Euthyphro.
textes.Aristophane le montre suspendu dans un p: Aristophanes showed him hanging in a basket to observe the sky in The Clouds, staged in 423 BC and placed last in the contest. In the Apology, Plato suggests the play weighed on the trial of 399.
textes.L'allégorie occupe le livre VII de la Ré: The allegory takes up Book VII of the Republic: Socrates tells it to Glaucon, Plato's brother, right after the images of the Sun and the line, to show the effect of education on our nature.
textes.Aristote fonde le Lycée vers 335 av. J.-: Aristotle founded the Lyceum around 335 BC, in a sanctuary of Apollo Lyceus. He taught while walking, hence the name Peripatetics. The Lyceum fell with Athens in 86 BC; its ruins were found in 1996, during digging for a museum.
textes.Héraclite d'Éphèse, actif vers 500 av. J: Heraclitus of Ephesus, active around 500 BC, was nicknamed "the Obscure" for his riddling style. According to Diogenes Laërtius, he deposited his only book in the Temple of Artemis; only fragments quoted by others survive.
textes.Zénon était un marchand chypriote. Après: Zeno was a Cypriot merchant. After a shipwreck, he read Xenophon's Memorabilia about Socrates in an Athens bookshop, and was sent to study with the Cynic Crates.
textes.Épicure fonde le Jardin à Athènes vers 3: Epicurus founded the Garden in Athens around 306 BC; the school welcomed many women, such as Themista and Leontion. His followers carved on their graves "I was not, I was, I am not, I do not care".
textes.Fils du médecin du roi Amyntas de Macédo: Son of King Amyntas of Macedon's physician, Aristotle taught Alexander at Mieza, in the gardens of the Nymphs near Pella. In 322 BC, accused of impiety, he left Athens "so as not to let the Athenians sin twice against philosophy", a nod to Socrates.
textes.Accusé par Mélétos, Anytos et Lycon, Soc: Accused by Meletus, Anytus and Lycon, Socrates was found guilty by 280 votes to 221. He first proposed, provocatively, to be fed at public expense in the Prytaneum, like a benefactor.
textes.Diogène et son père auraient été chassés: Diogenes and his father were said to have been driven from Sinope for debasing the currency. When Alexander asked what he wanted, he told him to stand out of his sun; when Plato defined man as a "featherless biped", he brought him a plucked cock.
textes.Les Premiers Analytiques datent d'enviro: The Prior Analytics date from around 350 BC. Aristotle's logic dominated for more than two thousand years: Kant still judged it "completed" in 1800, before Boole (1854) and then Frege (1879) went beyond it.
textes.Né à Cordoue en 1126, Averroès est juge: Born in Córdoba in 1126, Averroes was a judge and physician at the Almohad court. In 1195, his books were burned and he was exiled to Lucena. Dante placed him in Limbo, and Raphael painted him in The School of Athens.
textes.L'idée est bien plus ancienne qu'Ockham: The idea is much older than Ockham: Aristotle, Ptolemy and Robert Grosseteste already preferred the simplest explanation. The phrase "entities must not be multiplied without necessity" comes from John Punch in 1639, and Libert Froidmont claimed to have coined "Occam's razor" in 1649.
textes.Ses frères l'enlèvent et le gardent pris: His brothers kidnapped him and held him prisoner for nearly a year to stop him joining the Dominicans. His fellow students called him "the dumb ox". In December 1273, after a mystical experience, he stopped writing: it all seemed "like straw" to him. He was canonised in 1323.
textes.Le mythe naît au XIXe siècle : Washingto: The myth was born in the 19th century: Washington Irving published a romanticised biography of Christopher Columbus in 1828, mistaken for a scholarly work, and Antoine Letronne wrongly attributed a flat Earth to the Church Fathers in 1834.
textes.Machiavel l'écrit en 1513, quelques mois: Machiavelli wrote it in 1513, a few months after being arrested, tortured and banished by the returning Medici, and yet dedicated it to Lorenzo de' Medici. The book came out after his death, in 1532, and the Church placed it on the Index in 1559.
textes.Élevé en latin comme langue maternelle,: Raised with Latin as his first language, Montaigne withdrew in 1571, at 38, to the tower of his château, which he dedicated by an inscription to "his freedom, tranquility and leisure". He was nonetheless mayor of Bordeaux from 1581 to 1585.
textes.Érasme l'écrit en 1509 chez son ami Thom: Erasmus wrote it in 1509 at his friend Thomas More's house in London. The Latin title, Moriae Encomium, is a pun: it can also be read "In Praise of More". Hans Holbein the Younger illustrated a copy.
textes.Écrite en latin, Utopia paraît en 1516 e: Written in Latin, Utopia came out in 1516 and was only translated into English in 1551. More also played on eu-topos, "the good place". On his island, property is held in common and people work about six hours a day.
textes.Né à Tunis en 1332, Ibn Khaldoun écrit l: Born in Tunis in 1332, Ibn Khaldun wrote the Muqaddimah over more than three years, sheltered by a Berber tribe. He met the conqueror Timur outside Damascus. Historian Arnold Toynbee called it "the greatest work of its kind".
textes.Le débat part d'une question laissée ouv: The debate began with a question Porphyry left open in the 3rd century: do genera and species exist in things or only in the mind? Boethius passed it on to the Middle Ages by translating his Isagoge; Roscelin answered that universals are mere vocal sounds.
textes.Bruno est détenu sept ans à Rome ; le ca: Bruno was held for seven years in Rome; Cardinal Bellarmine demanded that he recant, in vain. To his judges he reportedly said: "Perhaps you pronounce this sentence against me with greater fear than I receive it." His statue was unveiled at the site of the pyre on 9 June 1889.
textes.L'édition de 1580 ne compte que deux liv: The 1580 edition had only two books; that of 1588 added the third. Montaigne then annotated a copy by hand, the "Bordeaux Copy", kept at the city's municipal library.
textes.Saint Augustin avait déjà répondu aux sc: Saint Augustine had already answered the sceptics, in the early 5th century in The City of God: "If I am mistaken, I exist." Avicenna also proposed the "floating man" thought experiment, about self-awareness without any perception.
textes.Pierre de Fermat découvre la même idée d: Pierre de Fermat discovered the same idea independently, without publishing it, and Nicole Oresme was already using similar constructions in the 14th century. The two perpendicular axes only took hold after La Géométrie was translated into Latin in 1649.
textes.Les Pensées sont un recueil, publié aprè: The Pensées are a collection, published after his death, of notes Pascal had never published: that is where the wager first appears in writing.
textes.Le 27 juillet 1656, la communauté juive: On 27 July 1656, Amsterdam's Jewish community issued against Spinoza, aged 23, the harshest ban in its history, never lifted. He lived by grinding lenses and died in The Hague in 1677, aged 44; his friends then published his works.
textes.L'image est ancienne : Aristote compare: The image is old: Aristotle already compared the mind to a tablet with nothing written on it. In the 12th century, Ibn Tufail's novel Hayy ibn Yaqdhan follows a child who learns everything alone on an island; its 1671 Latin translation influenced Locke.
textes.Sextus Empiricus soulevait déjà la diffi: Sextus Empiricus already raised the difficulty in antiquity. Hume formulated it in 1739 in his Treatise of Human Nature, then in 1748: for him, it is habit, not reason, that makes us expect tomorrow.
textes.Evelyn Beatrice Hall écrit cette phrase: Evelyn Beatrice Hall wrote the sentence in The Friends of Voltaire, in the chapter on Helvétius, to illustrate Voltaire's attitude. It is still often attributed to him.
textes.Kant ne quitte guère Königsberg que pour: Kant hardly left Königsberg except to tutor in nearby towns, from 1748 to 1754. After long years of silence, he published the Critique of Pure Reason in 1781, at about 57.
textes.La formule vient du poète latin Horace,: The phrase comes from the Latin poet Horace, around 20 BC, in a letter to Lollius: "He who has begun is half done; dare to know; begin!" Melanchthon quoted it in 1518 in Wittenberg, and Foucault took up Kant's text in 1984.
textes.Le livre est interdit en France, mis à l: The book was banned in France, put on the Index and burned in Geneva; Rousseau had to flee to avoid prison. Voltaire, who criticised it, protested: to burn a book of argument is to admit you lack the wit to answer it.
textes.Le projet devait au départ traduire la C: The project was first meant to translate Englishman Ephraim Chambers's Cyclopaedia (1728). Suspended in 1752, then stripped of its privilege in 1759, the work went on in secret. The Chevalier de Jaucourt alone wrote about a quarter of the articles.
textes.En 1699, Nicolas Fatio de Duillier accus: In 1699, Nicolas Fatio de Duillier accused Leibniz of plagiarising Newton. The 1713 Royal Society report that sided with Newton was written by Newton himself. Yet it is Leibniz's notation, dy/dx, that prevailed.
textes.Popper oppose les théories qui font des: Popper contrasted theories making risky predictions with psychoanalysis and Marxism, whose followers explained away any fact after the event. His example: no list of white swans proves they all are, but a single black swan refutes the idea.
textes.Kuhn prend pour exemple le passage de l': Kuhn's example is the shift from Ptolemy's astronomy to Copernicus's, in 1543. Kant had already spoken in 1787 of a "revolution in the way of thinking".
textes.En 1885, sa sœur Elisabeth épouse Bernha: In 1885, his sister Elisabeth married Bernhard Förster, a nationalist and antisemite; Nietzsche did not attend the wedding. They founded the colony of Nueva Germania in Paraguay. Later she compiled The Will to Power, and Hitler attended her funeral in 1935. Recent work, however, questions the idea of deliberate falsification.
textes.Le Deuxième Sexe se serait vendu à envir: The Second Sex reportedly sold about 22,000 copies in its first week. The Vatican put it on the Index, where it remained until the Index was abolished in 1966. The first English translation, in 1953, cut whole passages.
textes.Eichmann est enlevé en Argentine par des: Eichmann was seized in Argentina by Israeli agents in 1960, tried in 1961 and executed in 1962. Arendt covered the trial for The New Yorker, where her report appeared in five articles. The book sparked fierce controversy, notably with Gershom Scholem.
textes.Russell trouve le paradoxe en mai 1901 e: Russell found the paradox in May 1901 while looking for a flaw in a proof by Cantor. Frege replied on 22 June 1902 and added an appendix to his book: nothing worse can befall a scientific writer than to see one of the foundations of his edifice shaken. Zermelo had found it around 1899, without publishing it.
textes.Sartre avait écrit le 14 octobre 1964 à: Sartre had written to the Nobel Institute on 14 October 1964 asking to be removed from the list. A prisoner of war in 1940, he had written his first play in a camp in Trier. On 19 April 1980, 50,000 Parisians followed his coffin.
textes.Sartre prononce cette conférence le 29 o: Sartre gave this lecture on 29 October 1945 at the Club Maintenant in Paris, before a packed hall. The text came out in 1946, and Sartre later regretted publishing it.
textes.Camus commence l'essai en 1940, pendant: Camus began the essay in 1940, during the fall of France. He starts from what he calls the only philosophical question that matters: must one kill oneself after recognising life's absurdity? His answer is no.
textes.Wittgenstein prend ses notes comme solda: Wittgenstein took his notes as a soldier in the First World War and finished the book on leave in summer 1918. The 1922 English edition had an introduction by Bertrand Russell. At the time he thought he had solved all of philosophy's problems.
textes.Élu au Collège de France fin 1969 à une: Elected to the Collège de France in late 1969 to a chair in the "history of systems of thought", Foucault co-founded the Prison Information Group in February 1971. He died of AIDS on 25 June 1984; his partner Daniel Defert then founded the AIDES charity.
textes.Le livre paraît chez l'éditeur Julius Sp: The book was published by Julius Springer with the date 1935 printed on it. Popper himself rewrote it in English: The Logic of Scientific Discovery came out in 1959.
textes.Philippa Foot imagine son tramway en réf: Philippa Foot devised her trolley while thinking about debates on abortion and the doctrine of double effect. A version already existed in 1905 in a questionnaire by Frank Chapman Sharp, and it was Judith Jarvis Thomson who named it the "trolley problem" in 1976.
textes.Bentham meurt le 6 juin 1832. Selon son: Bentham died on 6 June 1832. Following his will, his body was dissected and then preserved by Thomas Southwood Smith, dressed in his clothes; his real head, judged too macabre, was replaced with a wax one. In 2020, he was placed at the entrance of UCL's new Student Centre.
textes.Dans le même livre de 1785, Kant donne u: In the same 1785 book, Kant gave another formula: treat humanity, in yourself and in others, always also as an end and never merely as a means.
textes.L'éthique des vertus revient au premier: Virtue ethics came back to the fore with Elizabeth Anscombe's article "Modern Moral Philosophy" in 1958, then with Alasdair MacIntyre's After Virtue in 1981. The four cardinal virtues are already in Plato's Republic.
textes.L'idée est plus ancienne qu'Aristote : «: The idea is older than Aristotle: "Nothing in excess" was carved on the front of the temple at Delphi. It is also found in China in Confucius's way of the mean, and in the Buddha's "Middle Way".
textes.Singer écrit cet essai en 1971 face à la: Singer wrote this essay in 1971 in response to the starvation of refugees during the Bangladesh Liberation War. William MacAskill came across it in a seminar and later helped found the effective altruism movement.
textes.Richard Ryder lance le mot dans une broc: Richard Ryder launched the word in a privately printed pamphlet in Oxford in 1970, protesting against animal experimentation. He wrote: "Since Darwin, scientists have agreed that there is no 'magical' essential difference between humans and other animals."
textes.Une forme négative de la règle figure dé: A negative form of the rule already appears on an Egyptian papyrus from the Late Period (664-323 BC): "That which you hate to be done to you, do not do to another." It is also found in Hillel the Elder, in the Talmud, and in the Mahabharata.
textes.Le premier raisonnement connu de ce type: The first known reasoning of this kind is in the Summa Theologica, on self-defence: Thomas Aquinas allows that one may kill an attacker if one aims to defend oneself, not to kill.
textes.En 2010, Felipe De Brigard renverse l'ex: In 2010, Felipe De Brigard turned the experiment around: of students told they were already plugged in, 54% wanted to disconnect, but only 13% if told their real life was that of a maximum-security prisoner. He saw it mostly as status quo bias.
textes.Le site est lancé en 2016 par l'équipe d: The site was launched in 2016 by Iyad Rahwan's team at the MIT Media Lab. The results outline three broad cultural clusters: for example, East Asian countries spare the young less often than others.
textes.Hobbes écrit le Léviathan pendant la gue: Hobbes wrote Leviathan during the English Civil War. Historian Hugh Trevor-Roper summed it up: "The axiom, fear; the method, logic; the conclusion, despotism."
textes.Montesquieu publie le livre anonymement: Montesquieu published the book anonymously in Geneva, after about ten years of work; the Church put it on the Index in 1751. He describes the English system at length, and the work inspired the framers of the US Constitution.
textes.L'économiste William Vickrey avait décri: Economist William Vickrey had described the same thought experiment as early as 1945, and John Harsanyi formalised it in 1955, but to defend utilitarianism. Rawls coined the phrases "original position" and "veil of ignorance".
textes.Pour écrire Les Politiques, Aristote fai: To write the Politics, Aristotle had 158 constitutions of Greek cities collected to compare their strengths and weaknesses. The text may come partly from students' notes taken at the Lyceum.
textes.En 1831, Tocqueville part avec Gustave d: In 1831, Tocqueville left with Gustave de Beaumont to study American prisons for the French government. They stayed about nine months and used the trip to observe the whole of society. The book came out in two parts, in 1835 and 1840.
textes.Mill conçoit l'essai en 1854 avec sa fem: Mill conceived the essay in 1854 with his wife Harriet Taylor, and they rewrote it together. She died suddenly in 1858; Mill published it the following year without changing it, to "consecrate it to her memory", calling it their joint production.
textes.Marx écrit ces notes à Bruxelles en 1845: Marx wrote these notes in Brussels in 1845 and did not publish them. Engels edited them and published them in 1888; the original text only appeared in 1924.
textes.Montaigne affirmait que son ami l'avait: Montaigne claimed his friend wrote it at 16 or 18, but the text more likely dates from 1552-1553, when La Boétie was 22. It circulated in copies and was only printed in 1576, after his death; the Huguenots took it up.
textes.Popper le formule dans une note de La So: Popper set it out in a note to The Open Society and Its Enemies: "Unlimited tolerance must lead to the disappearance of tolerance." He linked it to a "paradox of freedom" noted by Plato. Rawls, in 1971, called for tolerating the intolerant except when the free society's survival is at stake.
textes.Platon tente l'expérience en vrai : en 3: Plato tried it for real: in 367 BC, his disciple Dion invited him to Syracuse to advise the young tyrant Dionysius II. The pupil resisted, and nothing came of it. Later, the emperor Marcus Aurelius was seen as a philosopher king.
textes.Weber donne cette conférence le 28 janvi: Weber gave this lecture on 28 January 1919 in Munich, to a students' association, in the midst of the German Revolution. An extended version came out in July 1919.
textes.Thoreau refuse de payer l'impôt pour pro: Thoreau refused to pay the tax to protest against slavery and the war with Mexico. He made it into a lecture in 1848, then the essay Resistance to Civil Government in 1849.
textes.C'est la princesse Élisabeth de Bohême q: It was Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia who raised the awkward question, in a letter of 20 June 1643: how can an unextended soul move a body? Their correspondence lasted until Descartes's death in 1650.
textes.Galien la décrit le premier au IIe siècl: Galen first described it in the 2nd century, naming it konarion, "little cone". Descartes made it the "principal seat of the soul" in The Passions of the Soul (1649). Its hormone, melatonin, was only isolated in 1958 by Aaron Lerner at Yale.
textes.Leibniz imaginait déjà un cerveau agrand: Leibniz already imagined a brain enlarged to the size of a mill, where one would only see parts pushing each other. In 1961, a short story by Soviet writer Anatoly Dneprov had a whole stadium of people, who knew no Portuguese, simulate a translation program.
textes.Turing prédisait qu'autour de l'an 2000,: Turing predicted that around the year 2000, an average interrogator would have no more than a 70% chance of identifying the machine after five minutes. In 1966, the ELIZA program, which mimicked a psychotherapist, already fooled some users.
textes.L'article de Thomas Nagel paraît en octo: Thomas Nagel's article appeared in October 1974 in The Philosophical Review. Daniel Dennett noted that in 1950, B. A. Farrell had already raised a similar question in the journal Mind.
textes.Chalmers lance l'expression en 1994, dan: Chalmers launched the phrase in 1994, in a talk at the consciousness conference in Tucson, Arizona, before his 1995 article. Leibniz and Thomas Huxley had put forward similar arguments.
textes.Charles Sanders Peirce introduit le mot: Charles Sanders Peirce introduced the word quale in 1866, and C. I. Lewis used it in its modern sense in 1929. The "inverted spectrum" question comes from John Locke, in 1689.
textes.En 1925, C. D. Broad imaginait déjà un a: In 1925, C. D. Broad already imagined an archangel who knew everything about the structure of ammonia yet could not predict its smell. Jackson eventually changed his mind: in 2023 he said he no longer accepts his own argument.
textes.Hans Kornhuber et Lüder Deecke avaient d: Hans Kornhuber and Lüder Deecke had discovered this "readiness potential" in 1965. Libet also noted that the movement could still be cancelled: he spoke of "free won't". In 2012, Aaron Schurger and colleagues saw it rather as spontaneous fluctuations in neural activity.
textes.Selon Plutarque, les Athéniens gardèrent: According to Plutarch, the Athenians kept the ship until the time of Demetrius of Phalerum. In the 17th century, Thomas Hobbes made the puzzle harder: what if a second ship were rebuilt from the old planks taken out?
textes.Hilary Putnam en propose la première ver: Hilary Putnam proposed the first version in the 1960s, comparing the mind to a Turing machine. By the mid-1970s he himself began to question it, and Ned Block countered in 1980 with a "brain" made of the whole population of China.
textes.Le scénario vient de Gilbert Harman en 1: The scenario comes from Gilbert Harman in 1973. Putnam took it up in 1981 to argue that the sentence "I am a brain in a vat" refutes itself. Zhuangzi's butterfly dream already raises a similar question.
textes.Russell racontait l'histoire d'un poulet: Russell told the story of a chicken fed every day by the man who, one fine morning, wrings its neck. Hume had posed the problem in 1739; in 1955, Nelson Goodman invented a variant with the predicate "grue".
textes.Le manifeste du cercle paraît en 1929. M: The circle's manifesto appeared in 1929. Moritz Schlick was murdered in 1936 by a former student, and Nazi Germany's annexation of Austria in 1938 ended the circle in Vienna.
textes.Pierre Duhem limitait cette idée à la ph: Pierre Duhem limited this idea to physics. Quine extended it to all knowledge, including logic and mathematics, in "Two Dogmas of Empiricism", before partly backing down on logic.
textes.Le livre devait être un débat avec Imre: The book was meant to be a debate with Imre Lakatos, who would defend scientific reason while Feyerabend attacked it; Lakatos died suddenly in 1974. Feyerabend explained that "anything goes" is not his principle, but the terrified exclamation of a rationalist who takes a closer look at history.
textes.Les médecins hippocratiques voulaient dé: Hippocratic physicians already wanted to distinguish their reasoning from mythical accounts. In 1983, Larry Laudan judged that philosophy had failed to draw this line and proposed speaking instead of reliable or unreliable knowledge.
textes.Né Imre Lipsitz en Hongrie en 1922, Laka: Born Imre Lipsitz in Hungary in 1922, Lakatos changed his name to escape the Nazis, spent three years in prison under the communist regime, then fled in 1956. A professor at the London School of Economics, he died suddenly in 1974. His motto: philosophy of science without history of science is empty.
textes.Galilée avait déjà vu Neptune fin 1612 e: Galileo had already seen Neptune in late 1612 and early 1613, but took it for a star. Galle received Le Verrier's letter on the morning of 23 September 1846 and found the planet that very night, with Heinrich d'Arrest. Englishman John Couch Adams had made a similar calculation, hence a priority dispute.
textes.Cette idée est surtout associée à Hanson: This idea is mainly associated with Hanson, Kuhn and Feyerabend, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Pierre Duhem had probably already put it forward, at least implicitly, some fifty years earlier.
textes.L'article s'intitule « Transgresser les: The article was titled "Transgressing the Boundaries: Towards a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity" and appeared in a special issue on the "Science Wars". Sokal revealed the hoax about three weeks later in the magazine Lingua Franca. In 2018, the "grievance studies" affair replayed it.
textes.Les projets Many Labs du Center for Open: The Many Labs projects of the Center for Open Science followed: 186 researchers from 60 labs re-tested 28 psychology findings, and half failed to replicate, despite large samples.
textes.Le nom latin experimentum crucis est ens: The Latin name experimentum crucis was later coined by Robert Hooke, and Newton used it in the Opticks for the prism experiment showing that white light is made of different rays.
textes.{comp}. Socrate posait des questions jus: {comp}. Socrates asked questions until people admitted they knew nothing. Your turn.
textes.Philosophie. Kant n'a presque jamais qui: Philosophy. Kant hardly ever left Königsberg. You won't leave this trial without {comp}.
textes.Diogène cherchait un homme en plein jour: Diogenes looked for a man in broad daylight with a lantern. I'm looking for a right answer. {comp}.
textes.Juste. Descartes doutait de tout. Moi, j: Right. Descartes doubted everything. I doubt you less and less.
textes.Bonne réponse. Ockham vous félicite, san: Correct. Ockham congratulates you, with no superfluous entities.
textes.Correct. Montaigne aurait écrit un essai: Correct. Montaigne would have written an essay about you. A short one.
textes.Sage réponse. Je vais devoir trouver une: A wise answer. I'll have to find a deeper taunt.
textes.Raté. Socrate disait savoir qu'il ne sav: Missed. Socrates said he knew that he knew nothing. You're proving it.
textes.Faux. Diogène se roulait dans le sable b: Wrong. Diogenes rolled in hot sand to toughen himself. I'll let you roll in your error.
textes.Erreur. Thalès, dit-on, mesurait les pyr: Error. Thales, they say, measured the pyramids by their shadow. You didn't see yours coming.
textes.La caverne de Platon vous va bien. Reste: Plato's cave suits you. Stay there for a review.
textes.Précepteur d'Alexandre, il a écrit sur l: Tutor to Alexander, he wrote on logic, physics, biology, politics and rhetoric. He thought women had fewer teeth than men. Bertrand Russell was amused that he never thought to check in his two wives' mouths.
textes.Il enseigne la morale, les rites et l'ar: He taught morality, rites and the art of governing by example. His disciples collected his sayings in the Analects. “What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others” appears there, five centuries before the Gospels.
textes.Juge et médecin à Cordoue, il commente A: A judge and physician in Córdoba, he commented on Aristotle so completely that the Latins simply called him “the Commentator”. For him, philosophy and religion, properly interpreted, cannot contradict each other. Exiled, his books burned, he was rehabilitated shortly before his death.
textes.Diplomate, juge et historien né à Tunis,: A diplomat, judge and historian born in Tunis, he wrote the Muqaddimah in 1377, an introduction to history. In it he seeks the laws of the rise and fall of dynasties: a group's solidarity carries it to power, then luxury wears it down in three or four generations.
textes.En 1929, à 21 ans, elle est reçue deuxiè: In 1929, at 21, she placed second in the philosophy agrégation, the youngest of her year. Sartre came first, on his second attempt; the jury hesitated to swap them. Twenty years later, The Second Sex: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.”
textes.Pour lui, l'esprit et le corps sont deux: For him, mind and body are two distinct substances, which communicate through the pineal gland, in the middle of the brain. The question of their union has occupied philosophers ever since. His body rests in Saint-Germain-des-Prés; a skull presented as his is kept at the National Museum of Natural History.
textes.Pour lui, une théorie n'est scientifique: For him, a theory is only scientific if you can imagine the observation that would refute it. Astrology, which can accommodate anything, fails the test. In 1946 in Cambridge, Wittgenstein reportedly threatened him with a poker during a debate; the witnesses still disagree about what happened.
textes.Maîtriser les philosophes de l'Antiquité: Master the philosophers of Antiquity. The AI gives you back your jar.
textes.Diogène vivait dans un pithos, une jarre: Diogenes lived in a pithos, an earthenware jar. Alexander the Great supposedly asked him what he wanted; he supposedly replied: “Stand out of my sunlight.”
textes.Maîtriser le Moyen Âge et la Renaissance: Master the Middle Ages and the Renaissance. Christopher Columbus didn't convince anyone the Earth was round: everyone knew.
textes.Le mythe d'un Moyen Âge persuadé que la: The myth of a Middle Ages convinced the Earth was flat owes much to Washington Irving's fictionalized biography of Columbus, in 1828. Medieval scholars opposed Columbus over the size of the Earth, and they were right: he had underestimated it.
textes.Maîtriser l'âge classique et les Lumière: Master the classical age and the Enlightenment. The AI disapproves of your quotes, but lets you say them.
textes.« Je désapprouve ce que vous dites, mais: “I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it” is by Evelyn Beatrice Hall, in The Friends of Voltaire (1906). She was summing up Voltaire's thinking, and had to clarify it herself in 1939.
textes.Maîtriser les philosophes modernes. Votr: Master the modern philosophers. Your achievement is provisional, like any scientific theory.
textes.Le critère de la scientificité d'une thé: The criterion of the scientific status of a theory is its falsifiability, or refutability, or testability.
Master the first diamond of Wisdom. You now know that you know nothing, but with references.
I know that I know nothing.
textes.Réussir 3 quiz de Sagesse sans faute. Vo: Pass 3 Wisdom quizzes without a mistake. You finally see the objects, not their shadows.
textes.Platon place l'allégorie de la caverne a: Plato places the allegory of the cave in Book VII of the Republic. According to tradition, he had “Let no one ignorant of geometry enter here” inscribed over the door of the Academy. The phrase is only attested nearly nine centuries later.
textes.Maîtriser 9 compétences. L'arbre de la P: Master 9 skills. The Philosophy tree opens.
textes.Une vie sans examen ne vaut pas d'être v: The unexamined life is not worth living.
textes.Maîtriser l'éthique. Vous pouvez tirer l: Master ethics. You can pull the lever or do nothing. The AI has already chosen.
textes.Le dilemme du tramway, qui fonce sur cin: The trolley dilemma, hurtling toward five people unless you throw a switch toward just one, was posed in 1967 by the philosopher Philippa Foot, in a paper on abortion. The name “trolley problem” comes from Judith Jarvis Thomson, in 1976.
textes.Maîtriser la philosophie politique. La f: Master political philosophy. The end doesn't justify made-up quotes.
textes.« La fin justifie les moyens » ne figure: “The end justifies the means” appears nowhere in Machiavelli. In The Prince, he writes that in politics, with no court to appeal to, a prince is judged by his results. The more brutal phrase is a summary by his opponents.
textes.Maîtriser la philosophie de l'esprit. Vo: Master the philosophy of mind. Your cells change, so do your memories. Are you still you?
textes.Selon Plutarque, les Athéniens remplaçai: According to Plutarch, the Athenians replaced the rotten planks of Theseus's ship one by one: was it still the same ship? Hobbes, in 1655, sharpens the question: if someone rebuilds a ship from the old planks, which of the two is the real one?
textes.Maîtriser la philosophie des sciences. C: Master the philosophy of science. Shift your paradigm. Which one? Take your pick.
textes.Thomas Kuhn popularise en 1962 le mot «: Thomas Kuhn popularized the word “paradigm” in 1962. In 1970, the philosopher Margaret Masterman found twenty-one different senses of the word in his book. Kuhn acknowledged it, and came to prefer “disciplinary matrix”.
textes.La méthode scientifique, la cellule, l'é: The scientific method, the cell, evolution and genetics.
textes.Les plus anciennes traces de feu contrôl: The oldest traces of controlled fire are about a million years old (Wonderwerk Cave, in South Africa), but its regular use became widespread some 400,000 years ago. Cooking food makes it easier to digest: the anthropologist Richard Wrangham even sees it as a driver of the growth of our brain. No one “invented” fire one fine morning: it was tamed, lost and rekindled over hundreds of thousands of years.
textes.Case départ. Vos ancêtres ont mis des ce: Starting square. Your ancestors took hundreds of thousands of years to master fire. The AI gives you a little less time for what comes next.
textes.Les rois Ptolémées fondent à Alexandrie: The Ptolemaic kings founded the Museum and its library in Alexandria, which aimed to gather every book in the world. According to Galen, ships entering the port had to let their scrolls be copied, and the library sometimes kept the original and returned the copy. It is said to have held hundreds of thousands of scrolls, a figure reported by ancient authors and highly uncertain.
textes.Une bibliothèque qui gardait les origina: A library that kept the originals and returned the copies. The AI respects this very personal notion of borrowing.
textes.La même année que Copernic, André Vésale: The same year as Copernicus, Andreas Vesalius published De humani corporis fabrica, an anatomy treatise with magnificent plates. By dissecting himself, he corrected errors by Galen, who had dissected monkeys rather than humans. Before him, the professor read Galen from the chair while a barber did the cutting; Vesalius picked up the scalpel.
textes.Pendant treize siècles, on a décrit l'hu: For thirteen centuries, humans were described from monkeys. The AI makes no comment. She smiles.
textes.Vésale ouvre le corps humain : soixante: Vesalius opens the human body: sixty percent water, a little calcium, a pinch of iron. Atoms escape from the dissecting table.
textes.Robert Hooke publie Micrographia, rempli: Robert Hooke published Micrographia, filled with engravings made under the microscope: a fly's eye, a giant flea on a fold-out plate, and a thin slice of cork made of little chambers he called “cells.” Samuel Pepys stayed up until 2 a.m. reading it. Hooke quarreled with Newton over the priority of several discoveries, and no reliable portrait of him has come down to us.
textes.Hooke a vu les cellules en premier, et i: Hooke saw cells first, and no portrait of him remains. History is cruel. The AI is taking notes.
textes.Antoni van Leeuwenhoek, drapier à Delft: Antoni van Leeuwenhoek, a draper in Delft with no scholarly training, ground tiny lenses that magnified up to 275 times. From 1674, he saw “little animals” moving in water, and in 1676 he described them to the Royal Society. The skeptical London scholars sent witnesses to Delft. In 1677, they confirmed it.
textes.Un drapier sans diplôme découvre les mic: A draper with no degree discovers microbes. The AI reminds the graduates present that this is no excuse.
textes.Le Suédois Carl von Linné publie Systema: The Swede Carl Linnaeus published Systema naturae and sorted living things into kingdoms, classes, orders, genera and species. He imposed a two-word Latin name, such as Homo sapiens, “wise man,” which he coined in 1758. He also knew how to take revenge: he named a small weed after Siegesbeck, a botanist who had criticized his work.
textes.Homo sapiens, l'homme sage. Linné était: Homo sapiens, wise man. Linnaeus was an optimist. The AI has read your history.
textes.On disait dans les campagnes anglaises q: In the English countryside, it was said that milkmaids who had had cowpox, a mild disease of cows, did not catch smallpox. The doctor Edward Jenner put the idea to the test: on May 14, 1796, he inoculated young James Phipps with cowpox taken from a milkmaid's hand, then, in July, with smallpox: the boy did not fall ill. The word vaccine comes from variolae vaccinae, “cow pox,” from the Latin vacca. Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980.
textes.Le mot vaccin vient de la vache. Retenez: The word vaccine comes from the cow. Remember it, the AI might ask you. She will.
textes.Jenner a refusé de s'enrichir avec sa dé: Jenner refused to get rich from his discovery. He's giving you the same kind of gift.
textes.Après vingt ans de notes, Charles Darwin: After twenty years of notes, Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species, prompted by the manuscript of Alfred Russel Wallace, who had found the same idea: natural selection. The first printing of 1,250 copies was entirely taken up by booksellers two days before publication. Darwin only used the word “evolution” in the sixth edition, and “survival of the fittest” is a phrase by Herbert Spencer.
Darwin waited twenty years to publish. Your review that's two days late has no such excuse.
textes.Darwin a publié six éditions de L'Origin: Darwin published six editions of On the Origin of Species and only added “survival of the fittest” in the fifth. Revising is scientific.
textes.Le moine Gregor Mendel croise des millie: The monk Gregor Mendel crossed thousands of pea plants in the garden of his monastery in Brno and found laws of heredity: traits that come back in regular proportions, such as 3 to 1. He published in 1866 in a local journal, to no response. His work was rediscovered in 1900. In 1936, the statistician Ronald Fisher noted that his results were almost too perfect, a suspicion that more recent studies have largely dismissed.
textes.Les résultats de Mendel étaient trop bea: Mendel's results were too good to be true, according to Fisher. Yours don't have that problem.
textes.Avec ses flacons à col de cygne, Louis P: With his swan-neck flasks, Louis Pasteur had shown around 1860 that no microbe appears spontaneously in a sterile broth. In 1885, he vaccinated young Joseph Meister, bitten by a rabid dog, against rabies: the boy survived. The historian Gerald Geison showed, from his notebooks, that Pasteur had embellished the account of some trials: before Meister, he had vaccinated only 11 dogs, not 50 as he implied.
textes.Pasteur a vaincu la rage et un peu arran: Pasteur defeated rabies and touched up his notebooks a little. The AI retouches nothing. Play again.
textes.James Watson et Francis Crick proposent: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double helix structure of DNA. They relied notably on “Photo 51,” an X-ray image taken by Raymond Gosling in Rosalind Franklin's laboratory, which was shown to them without her consent. Watson, Crick and Maurice Wilkins received the Nobel in 1962; Franklin, who died in 1958, could no longer be awarded it.
textes.La double hélice doit beaucoup à une pho: The double helix owes a lot to a photo shown without permission. The AI always asks before judging you. No, actually.
textes.Le cliché 51 de Rosalind Franklin a guid: Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51 guided Watson and Crick to the double helix, but her role stayed in the shadows for decades. Back to the first square you left in the shadows.
textes.Une hypothèse scientifique doit pouvoir: A scientific hypothesis must be refutable by an observation (Popper).
textes.Groupe témoin : on compare avec un group: Control group: you compare with an identical group that doesn't receive the treatment, double-blind if possible.
textes.Un résultat compte quand il est reprodui: A result counts when other teams reproduce it.
textes.Une théorie scientifique n'est pas une s: A scientific theory isn't a mere guess: it's a tested framework that explains many observations.
textes.Mille observations favorables ne prouven: A thousand favorable observations don't prove a hypothesis; a single solid contrary observation can refute it.
textes.Le cycle de la méthode scientifique: The cycle of the scientific method
textes.La cellule est l'unité du vivant. Les pr: The cell is the unit of life. Prokaryotes (bacteria) have no nucleus; eukaryotes have one.
textes.Le noyau contient l'ADN ; les mitochondr: The nucleus contains DNA; mitochondria produce energy (ATP); ribosomes make proteins.
textes.Les cellules végétales ont en plus une p: Plant cells also have a wall and chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
textes.Mitose : une cellule donne deux cellules: Mitosis: one cell gives two identical cells. Meiosis: it gives four gametes with half as many chromosomes.
textes.Les mitochondries ne fabriquent pas l'én: Mitochondria don't make energy out of nothing: they draw it from glucose and oxygen.
textes.Sélection naturelle, mutations, histoire: Natural selection, mutations, the history of life.
textes.Sélection naturelle : les individus port: Natural selection: individuals carrying advantageous variations leave more offspring.
textes.Les mutations sont aléatoires ; la sélec: Mutations are random; selection is not.
textes.L'humain ne descend pas du chimpanzé : i: Humans aren't descended from chimpanzees: they share a common ancestor, who lived several million years ago.
textes.L'évolution agit sur des populations sur: Evolution acts on populations over generations, not on an individual during its lifetime.
textes.La girafe n'a pas allongé son cou à forc: The giraffe didn't lengthen its neck by stretching it: that's Lamarck, and it's wrong.
textes.Gènes, allèles, hérédité, ADN et mutatio: Genes, alleles, heredity, DNA and mutations.
textes.Un gène existe en plusieurs versions, le: A gene comes in several versions, alleles. You get one from each parent.
textes.Un allèle dominant s'exprime dès qu'il e: A dominant allele shows as soon as it's present; a recessive allele only in two copies.
textes.Deux parents Aa ont une chance sur quatr: Two Aa parents have a one-in-four chance of having an aa child.
textes.L'ADN humain compte environ 3 milliards: Human DNA has about 3 billion base pairs and 20,000 protein-coding genes.
textes.Dominant ne veut pas dire fréquent : la: Dominant doesn't mean common: polydactyly is dominant and rare.

textes.Organes, circulation, respiration, diges: Organs, circulation, breathing, digestion and skeleton.
textes.Le cœur a deux circuits : la petite circ: The heart has two circuits: the pulmonary circulation to the lungs, the systemic to the rest of the body.
textes.Les échanges d'oxygène se font dans les: Oxygen exchange takes place in the pulmonary alveoli, about 70 m² of surface.
textes.La digestion chimique commence dans la b: Chemical digestion starts in the mouth and most absorption takes place in the small intestine.
textes.Un adulte a 206 os ; un nouveau-né en a: An adult has 206 bones; a newborn has more, which fuse as they grow.
textes.Le sang n'est jamais bleu : il est rouge: Blood is never blue: it's dark red in the veins; the blue color comes from the skin filtering light.
textes.Bactéries, virus, vaccins, antibiotiques: Bacteria, viruses, vaccines, antibiotics and the body's defenses.
textes.Les bactéries sont des cellules vivantes: Bacteria are living cells; viruses only reproduce inside a cell.
textes.Les antibiotiques tuent les bactéries ma: Antibiotics kill bacteria but have no effect on viruses.
textes.Un vaccin entraîne le système immunitair: A vaccine trains the immune system with a fragment or a harmless version of the microbe; immune memory remains.
textes.Immunité collective : quand assez de gen: Herd immunity: when enough people are immune, the microbe stops circulating, which protects those who can't be vaccinated.
textes.Prendre des antibiotiques contre un rhum: Taking antibiotics for a cold does nothing and favors resistant bacteria.
textes.Chaînes alimentaires, cycles de la matiè: Food chains, matter cycles, biodiversity and climate.

textes.Les décomposeurs ne sont pas les « éboue: Decomposers aren't optional “garbage collectors”: without them, the matter cycles stop.

textes.CRISPR-Cas9 coupe l'ADN à un endroit pré: CRISPR-Cas9 cuts DNA at a precise spot guided by an RNA: it's programmable scissors.
textes.Un vaccin à ARN messager donne aux cellu: A messenger RNA vaccine gives cells the recipe for a viral protein; the RNA is broken down within a few days and doesn't enter the nucleus.
textes.Cloner, c'est obtenir un organisme génét: Cloning means obtaining a genetically identical organism (Dolly the sheep, 1996).
textes.Un vaccin à ARN ne modifie pas l'ADN : i: An RNA vaccine doesn't change DNA: it doesn't enter the nucleus.
textes.Un cycle de PCR : chaque tour double le: One PCR cycle: each round doubles the number of copies
Scientific = falsifiable (Popper, 1934). A thousand confirmations do not prove; one solid exception refutes.
You have seen a thousand swans, all white. Can you claim all swans are white? No: you would have to have seen them all. But a single black swan is enough to refute the sentence. That is the asymmetry Karl Popper set out in 1934: you never prove a general law for good, but you can catch it out.
textes.D'où son critère : une hypothèse est sci: Hence his criterion: a hypothesis is scientific if some observation could contradict it. "It will rain or it will not rain tomorrow" risks nothing, so it teaches nothing. A theory that makes risky predictions and survives the tests is better than one that forbids nothing. And the word theory, in science, is not a guess: it is a well-tested framework, like the theory of evolution.
textes.Groupe témoin tiré au sort, placebo, dou: Randomised control group, placebo, double blind, then replication by other teams.
textes.Semmelweis (1847) : lavage des mains, mo: Semmelweis (1847): handwashing, mortality from 18 % to under 2 %, rejected for lack of an explanation. Data first.
textes.En 1847, à l'hôpital général de Vienne,: In 1847, at the Vienna General Hospital, Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that women delivered by doctors died of childbed fever far more often than those delivered by midwives. The doctors often came straight from autopsies. He imposed handwashing with chlorinated lime: mortality, 18.3 % in April 1847, fell to 1.2 % in July.
textes.Ses collègues le rejettent : il n'a pas: His colleagues rejected him: he had no explanation, and the idea that doctors were killing their patients offended them. It took the work of Pasteur and Koch on germs, a few decades later, to understand why he was right. The lesson: a solid result can come before its explanation, and authority is no substitute for data.
textes.La cellule, brique du vivant: The cell, the brick of life
textes.Procaryote = sans noyau (bactéries) ; eu: Prokaryote = no nucleus (bacteria); eukaryote = nucleus. Plants add a wall and chloroplasts. A virus is not a cell.
textes.En 1665, Robert Hooke regarde une fine t: In 1665 Robert Hooke looked at a thin slice of cork under the microscope and saw little chambers: he called them cells. We have known since that every living thing is made of cells, a single one for a bacterium to tens of trillions for a human.
textes.Il en existe deux grands types. Les proc: There are two broad types. Prokaryotes, like bacteria, have no nucleus: their DNA floats in the cell. Eukaryotes, animals, plants, fungi, keep their DNA in a nucleus. Plant cells also have a rigid wall, a large vacuole and chloroplasts for photosynthesis. Viruses are not cells: without a cell to hijack, they can do nothing.
textes.ADN (noyau) → ARN messager → protéine (r: DNA (nucleus) → messenger RNA → protein (ribosomes). Same DNA everywhere, different genes switched on.
textes.Toutes vos cellules portent à peu près l: All your cells carry more or less the same DNA. A neuron and a skin cell do not differ in their genome, but in the genes they switch on. An ordinary human cell has 46 chromosomes, in 23 pairs.
textes.Mitochondries : énergie (ATP) tirée du g: Mitochondria: energy (ATP) drawn from glucose and oxygen. They are former bacteria (Margulis, 1967).
textes.Les mitochondries tirent l'énergie du gl: Mitochondria draw energy from glucose and oxygen and store it as ATP: they are the cell's power plants. They make nothing from nothing; they slowly burn what you eat with the air you breathe.
textes.Leur origine est étonnante : ce sont d'a: Their origin is surprising: they are former bacteria, swallowed long ago by another cell and never digested. The idea, sketched by Konstantin Mereschkowski in 1905, was defended with evidence by Lynn Margulis in 1967. The clues: mitochondria have their own DNA, circular like bacterial DNA, bacteria-like ribosomes, and divide on their own. Chloroplasts, for their part, descend from cyanobacteria.
textes.Variation + hérédité + reproduction inég: Variation + heredity + unequal reproduction = natural selection (Darwin, 1859; Wallace, 1858). Mutations random, selection not.
textes.Trois constats suffisent. Les individus: Three observations are enough. Individuals of a species vary. Part of that variation is passed on to offspring. And not all survive or reproduce equally. So, generation after generation, the variations that help leave offspring become more common. That is natural selection, published by Charles Darwin in 1859 in On the Origin of Species.
textes.Alfred Russel Wallace avait eu la même i: Alfred Russel Wallace had had the same idea; their two texts were read together at the Linnean Society of London in 1858. Mutations, the source of variation, happen at random; selection owes nothing to chance. And "survival of the fittest" means reproductive success, not strength: an antibiotic-resistant bacterium is "fit" simply because it survives the treatment.
textes.Les caractères acquis ne se transmettent: Acquired traits are not inherited (against Lamarck). Evolution acts on populations and has no goal.
textes.Version darwinienne : parmi les girafes,: The Darwinian version: among giraffes, some were born with slightly longer necks; if that helped them survive and reproduce, they left more offspring. Evolution acts on populations, over generations, never on an individual during its life. And it has no goal: some parasites have even lost organs over time.
textes.Humains et chimpanzés : un ancêtre commu: Humans and chimpanzees: a common ancestor 6 to 7 million years ago. Birds are dinosaurs.
textes.L'humain ne descend pas du chimpanzé act: Humans do not descend from today's chimpanzee. The two species share a common ancestor that lived about 6 to 7 million years ago; since then each line has evolved its own way. The chimpanzee is our cousin, not our grandfather.
textes.Les fossiles racontent ces embranchement: Fossils tell the story of these branchings. Tiktaalik, discovered in 2004, shows a transitional form between fish and four-legged animals. And birds are theropod dinosaurs, the only survivors of the extinction about 66 million years ago, probably caused by the Chicxulub asteroid.
textes.Mendel (1866) : deux versions de chaque: Mendel (1866): two versions of each gene, one from each parent. Rediscovered in 1900.
textes.De 1856 à 1863, dans le jardin de son ab: From 1856 to 1863, in the garden of his abbey in Brno, the monk Gregor Mendel crossed about 28,000 plants, mostly peas. He crossed yellow and green peas: the first generation was all yellow. But in the next generation green came back, in about a quarter of the plants.
textes.Il en déduit que chaque caractère dépend: He deduced that each trait depends on two "factors", one from each parent: our genes. He presented them in 1865, published them in 1866, and nobody took any notice. In 1900 three botanists, Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns and Erich von Tschermak, rediscovered his laws independently. Genetics was born, thirty-five years late.
textes.Dominant, récessif et le tableau des qua: Dominant, recessive and the four-square table
textes.Dominant : s'exprime avec une seule copi: Dominant: shows with one copy; recessive: with two. Aa × Aa → a quarter aa. Dominant ≠ common.
textes.Un gène existe en plusieurs versions, le: A gene comes in several versions, alleles. The dominant allele, written A, shows as soon as it is present; the recessive allele, a, only in two copies. A person who is Aa therefore carries the recessive trait without showing it, and can pass it on: it sometimes stays hidden for several generations.
textes.A avec T, G avec C. Double hélice : Wats: A with T, G with C. Double helix: Watson and Crick (1953), thanks to Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51.
textes.L'ADN s'écrit avec quatre lettres, les b: DNA is written with four letters, the bases A, T, G and C, and these letters always pair the same way: A with T, G with C. One strand is therefore enough to rebuild the other, and that is how the cell copies its DNA. The human genome has about 3 billion base pairs, and only about 20,000 protein-coding genes, far fewer than the 100,000 expected.
textes.En 1953, James Watson et Francis Crick p: In 1953 James Watson and Francis Crick published the double helix structure. They relied on Photo 51, an X-ray diffraction image taken in Rosalind Franklin's laboratory, without her knowledge. She died in 1958 and did not share the 1962 Nobel Prize. Today the CRISPR-Cas9 tool can correct this writing at a precise spot.
textes.Circulation en circuit fermé (Harvey, 16: Closed-circuit circulation (Harvey, 1628). Right heart → lungs; left heart → body. Blood is never blue.
textes.Pendant quatorze siècles, on a suivi Gal: For fourteen centuries people followed Galen: the liver made blood from food, and the body used it up. In 1628 William Harvey did a simple calculation, with deliberately low estimates: in one day the heart pumps far more than the body's weight. The liver cannot produce that. Blood must therefore go round in a closed circuit.
textes.Le cœur est une double pompe. La partie: The heart is a double pump. The right side sends blood to the lungs, the pulmonary circulation, where it picks up oxygen in about 70 m² of alveoli. The left side sends it round the whole body, the systemic circulation. And blood is never blue: it is dark red in the veins; it is the skin that makes them look blue.
textes.Bouche → estomac → intestin grêle (absor: Mouth → stomach → small intestine (absorption). Bile from the liver for fats. Kidneys: 180 L filtered a day.
textes.La digestion commence dans la bouche, où: Digestion begins in the mouth, where saliva already attacks starch. The stomach churns and acidifies. The liver makes bile, stored in the gallbladder, which helps digest fats. Most absorption then takes place in the small intestine, whose folded wall offers a very large surface.
textes.Les reins font le tri : ils filtrent env: The kidneys do the sorting: they filter about 180 litres of blood a day and pass only a small part of it as urine. The pancreas produces insulin, which lets sugar into the cells; its discovery in 1921 by Banting and Best transformed the lives of diabetics.
textes.Vésale (1543) corrige Galien en disséqua: Vesalius (1543) corrects Galen by dissecting humans. 206 adult bones, 4.5 to 6 L of blood. The 10 % myth is false.
textes.Galien avait surtout disséqué des animau: Galen had mostly dissected animals, notably macaques, and drawn from them a human anatomy full of mistakes that nobody dared contradict. In 1543 Andreas Vesalius published the Fabrica, illustrated with magnificent plates. He dissected human bodies, which was rare, and corrected Galen on many points: the lower jaw is a single bone, not two; the wall between the ventricles has no hole.
textes.Quelques chiffres de ce corps enfin rega: A few figures from this body finally looked at: 206 bones in an adult, about 300 in a newborn, which fuse as it grows; 4.5 to 6 litres of blood; a heart that beats 60 to 100 times a minute at rest. And no, we do not use only 10 % of our brain: imaging shows every area is used.
textes.Bactéries et virus, deux ennemis différe: Bacteria and viruses, two different enemies
textes.Bactérie = cellule vivante ; virus = par: Bacterium = living cell; virus = cell parasite. Antibiotics: bacteria only (Fleming, 1928).
textes.Une bactérie est une cellule vivante, qu: A bacterium is a living cell that feeds and divides on its own. A virus is just a genetic message in a shell: it has to get into a cell and hijack its machinery to copy itself. That difference decides the treatment.
textes.Les antibiotiques attaquent des mécanism: Antibiotics attack mechanisms specific to bacteria; against a virus, a cold or flu, they do nothing. In September 1928 Alexander Fleming came back from holiday and found a culture dish overrun by a mould, Penicillium, around which the bacteria had died: that was penicillin. In his Nobel lecture in 1945 he was already warning: misused, it would make microbes resistant.
textes.Vaccin = entraînement du système immunit: Vaccine = training the immune system, which keeps a memory (Jenner, 1796). Smallpox eradicated in 1980.
textes.En 1796, Edward Jenner inocule à un garç: In 1796 Edward Jenner inoculated a boy, James Phipps, with pus from cowpox, a mild disease of cows, then exposed him to smallpox: he did not fall ill. The word vaccine comes from this, from the Latin vacca, cow. Before him, people practised variolation, a risky inoculation with smallpox itself.
textes.Le principe : présenter au système immun: The principle: show the immune system a fragment or a harmless version of the microbe. It makes antibodies and keeps a memory, which lets it react fast at the real encounter. When enough people are immune, the microbe stops circulating and protects those who cannot be vaccinated. Smallpox, declared eradicated by the WHO in 1980, remains the only human disease beaten this way.
textes.Les antibiotiques sélectionnent les bact: Antibiotics select resistant bacteria. No antibiotic against a virus.
textes.Une bactérie se divise parfois toutes le: A bacterium sometimes divides every twenty minutes. In an infection there are billions, and a few carry by chance a mutation that makes them resistant to an antibiotic. The treatment kills the others; the resistant ones survive and multiply. That is natural selection, before our eyes.
textes.Producteurs → consommateurs → décomposeu: Producers → consumers → decomposers. About 10 % of the energy passes from one link to the next (Lindeman, 1942).
textes.Une chaîne alimentaire part des producte: A food chain starts with the producers, plants and algae, which build their matter from light, water and CO₂. Then come the consumers, herbivores then carnivores, and finally the decomposers, fungi and bacteria, which return dead matter to the soil. Without them the cycles would stop.
textes.À chaque maillon, la plus grande partie: At each link, most of the energy is lost, mainly through respiration: roughly only 10 % passes to the next level. This 10 % rule comes from Raymond Lindeman, in 1942. That is why it takes a lot of grass to feed a few gazelles, and a lot of gazelles for one lion: large predators are bound to be rare.
textes.La matière se recycle, l'énergie vient d: Matter is recycled; energy comes from the Sun and dissipates. Natural greenhouse effect, strengthened by our emissions (Arrhenius, 1896).
textes.La matière circule en cycles : le carbon: Matter moves in cycles: carbon goes from the air to plants, animals, soil, oceans, and back. Water evaporates, falls, runs off. Energy does not go round: it arrives from the Sun and ends up dissipated as heat.
textes.L'effet de serre est naturel et vital :: The greenhouse effect is natural and vital: without it the Earth would be frozen. But the CO₂ we emit reinforces it. Svante Arrhenius calculated its effect as early as 1896. The oceans absorb about a quarter of our CO₂ emissions, which acidifies them, and overheated corals expel the algae that feed them: they bleach.
textes.L'espèce qui tient tout: The species that holds it all
textes.Espèce clé de voûte : son retrait boulev: Keystone species: removing it upsets the ecosystem (Paine, 1969). Yellowstone wolves, 1995: trophic cascade.
textes.Certaines espèces pèsent bien plus que l: Some species weigh far more than their numbers. In the 1960s, on the coast of Washington State, the ecologist Robert Paine removed the starfish Pisaster from a stretch of shore: mussels, freed from their predator, took over everything, and the rock pools went from 15 species to 8 in three years. In 1969 he coined the term keystone species.
textes.Le loup de Yellowstone, réintroduit en 1: The Yellowstone wolf, reintroduced in 1995, is the famous example: by keeping elk in check, it is said to have let willows and aspens grow back along the rivers. That is a trophic cascade, although its real extent is still debated. Conversely, an invasive species, like the rabbit in Australia, can throw everything off balance.
textes.PCR : chauffer, refroidir, recopier ; ch: PCR: heat, cool, copy; each cycle doubles the DNA (30 cycles ≈ 1 billion). Mullis, 1983.
textes.La PCR copie un fragment d'ADN des milli: PCR copies a piece of DNA billions of times. Each cycle heats the DNA to around 95 °C to separate its two strands, cools it so that small primers attach, then lets an enzyme rebuild the missing strands at around 72 °C. Each cycle doubles the number of copies: after 30 cycles, a single molecule has produced over a billion.
textes.L'astuce : une enzyme qui résiste à la c: The trick: a heat-resistant enzyme, Taq polymerase, taken from a hot-spring bacterium, Thermus aquaticus, notably from Yellowstone. Kary Mullis invented the method in 1983 and received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1993. Diagnostic tests, criminal investigations, ancient DNA: it is everywhere.
textes.CRISPR-Cas9 : un ARN guide mène Cas9 cou: CRISPR-Cas9: a guide RNA leads Cas9 to cut DNA at a precise spot (Charpentier and Doudna, 2012; Nobel 2020).
textes.Les bactéries gardent en mémoire des mor: Bacteria keep pieces of DNA from viruses that have attacked them, so they can recognise and cut them up at the next attack. In 2012 Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna turned this system into a tool: a guide RNA leads the Cas9 enzyme to a chosen sequence, where it cuts the DNA.
textes.C'est un ciseau programmable, bien plus: It is programmable scissors, far simpler and cheaper than earlier methods. They received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020. This is not biologists' first ethical debate: as early as 1975, at Asilomar, they imposed a moratorium on themselves for the first genetic manipulations.
textes.Le vaccin qui donne une recette: The vaccine that hands over a recipe
textes.Vaccin à ARN : une recette de protéine,: mRNA vaccine: a protein recipe, read outside the nucleus, broken down within days. Does not alter DNA (Karikó and Weissman, Nobel 2023).
textes.Un vaccin à ARN messager ne contient pas: An mRNA vaccine does not contain the virus, but the recipe for one of its proteins. Cells read this message, make the protein, and the immune system learns to recognise it. The RNA stays outside the nucleus, where the DNA is, and breaks down within a few days: it does not alter the genome.
textes.Cette technique n'est pas née avec la co: This technique was not born with covid-19. Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman found in the 2000s how to make injected RNA less inflammatory; they received the Nobel Prize in 2023. Another milestone: since 1982, insulin for diabetics has been produced by genetically modified bacteria, no longer extracted from animal pancreases.
textes.Un malade prend un remède et guérit. Le: A patient takes a remedy and gets better. Did the remedy work? Impossible to say: they might have recovered on their own. To find out, you compare two similar groups, drawn by lot: one gets the treatment, the other a placebo, a pill with no active ingredient. Only the difference between the two counts. The ancestor of these trials dates from 20 May 1747: aboard HMS Salisbury, the Scottish doctor James Lind split twelve sailors with scurvy across six treatments. The two given oranges and lemons were almost recovered by the end of the month.
textes.En double aveugle, ni les patients ni le: In a double-blind trial, neither patients nor doctors know who receives what, so that their expectations do not skew the result. Random allocation took hold with the British streptomycin trial against tuberculosis, published in 1948, where the statistician Austin Bradford Hill had it adopted. And a result only really counts when other teams find it again: that is reproducibility. Even a peer-reviewed article can be corrected or retracted later.
textes.Le noyau garde l'ADN, la recette de tout: The nucleus keeps the DNA, the recipe for every protein. To make a protein, the cell copies the gene it needs into messenger RNA, which leaves the nucleus. Ribosomes read this message three letters at a time and assemble the amino acids in the right order. This one-way flow, from DNA to RNA to protein, was called the "central dogma" of molecular biology by Francis Crick in 1958; he returned to it in 1970 in Nature.
textes.Jean-Baptiste de Lamarck pensait que les: Jean-Baptiste de Lamarck thought organs change through use and that those changes are passed on: the giraffe would have lengthened its neck by stretching it, and bequeathed it to its young. He set it out in 1809 in his Zoological Philosophy, one of the first scientific theories of evolution. That is wrong: a muscular blacksmith does not have more muscular children. What you acquire in your life is not written into your genes.
textes.Deux parents Aa : chacun transmet A ou a: Two Aa parents: each passes on A or a, at random. The table gives AA, Aa, aA and aa. This grid bears the name of the English geneticist Reginald Punnett, who devised it around 1905, shortly after Mendel's work was rediscovered in 1900. On average one child in four is aa and shows the recessive trait. Careful: dominant does not mean common. Polydactyly, having extra fingers, is dominant and yet rare.
textes.D'où les règles : ne pas prendre d'antib: Hence the rules: do not take antibiotics against a virus, and finish the prescribed course, so as not to let the toughest bacteria survive. Alexander Fleming, who had discovered penicillin in 1928, was already warning in 1945, in his Nobel lecture: he feared that "the ignorant man" would underdose himself. Fever is not the enemy: it hinders the growth of some microbes and activates the defences.

He shows that arteries contain blood, not just air, and that nerves start from the brain: by tying off a pig's laryngeal nerve, he makes it lose its voice.
