textes.Le coefficient de corrélation a été mis: The correlation coefficient was developed by Karl Pearson from an idea Francis Galton introduced in the 1880s. The formula itself had been published by Auguste Bravais as early as 1844.
textes.Le 20 mai 1747, à bord du HMS Salisbury,: On 20 May 1747, aboard HMS Salisbury, physician James Lind split 12 sailors with scurvy into six pairs, each with a different remedy. Only those given citrus fruit really recovered: it was one of the first comparative trials in history.
textes.En 1835 à Nuremberg, un test de sel homé: In 1835 in Nuremberg, a test of diluted homeopathic salt run by Friedrich Wilhelm von Hoven was one of the first double-blind protocols. It challenged homeopathy.
textes.Popper visait des théories qui expliquai: Popper was targeting theories that explained everything, such as Freud's and Adler's psychoanalysis: in his view, a theory that rules out no observation predicts nothing. His 1934 book was only translated into English in 1959.
textes.« Placebo » est un mot latin qui veut di: "Placebo" is a Latin word meaning "I shall please". In 1955, a study with a now famous title, The Powerful Placebo, showed that the placebo effect really mattered in medicine.
textes.Le 23 mars 1989, Fleischmann et Pons ann: On 23 March 1989, Fleischmann and Pons announced cold fusion at a press conference. Laboratories around the world repeated the experiment and failed: the claim faded for lack of replication.
textes.Jacques Bernoulli a mis plus de 20 ans à: Jacob Bernoulli spent over 20 years proving the law of large numbers, published in 1713 in Ars Conjectandi. Poisson gave it the name "law of large numbers" in 1837.
textes.Guillaume d'Ockham, moine franciscain an: William of Ockham, an English Franciscan friar, lived c. 1287-1347. The phrase "Ockham's razor" only appeared centuries later: Libert Froidmont claimed to have coined it in 1649.
textes.La plus ancienne relecture avant publica: The oldest known pre-publication review dates from 1665, by Henry Oldenburg, founder of the Royal Society's Philosophical Transactions. Nature has only required outside reviewers since 1973.
textes.À la première clinique d'obstétrique de: At Vienna's First Obstetrical Clinic, mortality fell from 18.3% in April 1847 to 1.2% in July after washing with chlorinated lime. His colleagues still rejected him: it took Pasteur's germ theory to prove him right.
textes.Albert von Kölliker observe les mitochon: Albert von Kölliker observed mitochondria in insect muscles in 1857. Carl Benda named them in 1898, from the Greek for "thread-like granule". The "powerhouse" nickname dates from 1957.
textes.En 1683, Antoni van Leeuwenhoek décrit à: In 1683, Antonie van Leeuwenhoek described to the Royal Society bacteria taken from the human mouth, seen through his own microscopes. He called these tiny beings "little animals".
textes.Joseph Priestley montre qu'une plante «: Joseph Priestley showed that a plant "restores" air spoiled by a candle or a mouse. In 1779, Jan Ingenhousz repeated the experiment and found the key: sunlight is needed.
textes.En 1869 à Tübingen, Friedrich Miescher i: In 1869 in Tübingen, Friedrich Miescher isolated an unknown substance from the nuclei of white blood cells, taken from the pus on hospital bandages. He called it "nuclein": it was DNA.
textes.George Palade décrit les ribosomes en 19: George Palade described ribosomes in 1955 using the electron microscope. He received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1974 with Albert Claude and Christian de Duve.
textes.En 1958, John Gurdon clone une grenouill: In 1958, John Gurdon cloned a frog using nuclei from tadpole cells: the nucleus of an already specialised cell keeps the whole programme. He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize with Shinya Yamanaka.
textes.Pendant plus de 30 ans, on a cru que l'h: For more than 30 years, humans were believed to have 48 chromosomes, as counted by Theophilus Painter in 1921. On 22 December 1955, in Lund, Joe Hin Tjio and Albert Levan counted 46.
textes.Micrographia, le livre où Hooke nomme le: Micrographia, the book in which Hooke named cells, came out in January 1665 under the aegis of the Royal Society. Samuel Pepys called it "the most ingenious book that ever I read in my life".
textes.Oscar Hertwig décrit la méiose en 1876 d: Oscar Hertwig described meiosis in 1876 in sea urchin eggs. August Weismann explained its role in heredity in 1890, and the word "meiosis" was coined in 1905.
textes.En 1892, Dmitri Ivanovsky montre que l'a: In 1892, Dmitri Ivanovsky showed that the agent of tobacco mosaic disease passed through porcelain filters that stop bacteria. In 1898, Martinus Beijerinck saw it as a new kind of agent and called it a virus.
textes.Entre 1885 et 1901, le chimiste allemand: Between 1885 and 1901, German chemist Albrecht Kossel isolated and named the bases of nucleic acids: adenine, cytosine, guanine, thymine and uracil. Nobel Prize in Medicine 1910.
textes.En 1838, le chimiste français Anselme Pa: In 1838, French chemist Anselme Payen isolated the material of plant cell walls. The word "cellulose" appeared in 1839, in Jean-Baptiste Dumas's report on his memoir.
textes.L'Origine des espèces paraît le 24 novem: On the Origin of Species came out on 24 November 1859 from John Murray, in a print run of 1,250 copies. All available copies were taken up at the booksellers' sale, and a second edition followed in January 1860.
textes.En 1871, dans La Filiation de l'homme, D: In 1871, in The Descent of Man, Darwin applied evolution to our species. He explained the gap between humans and the other primates by intermediate forms that have died out.
textes.La sélection naturelle est présentée pou: Natural selection was first presented on 1 July 1858 at the Linnean Society of London, with an essay by Wallace and extracts from Darwin read together.
textes.En 1956, le géochimiste Clair Patterson: In 1956, geochemist Clair Patterson dated the Earth at 4.55 billion years, using lead from the Canyon Diablo meteorite. Along the way he discovered lead pollution, and later fought against leaded petrol.
textes.Le botaniste Hugo de Vries forge le mot: Botanist Hugo de Vries coined the word "mutation" for sudden variations, in The Mutation Theory (1901-1903). He had spotted them in evening primrose, found in an abandoned potato field.
textes.L'archéoptéryx, fossile à plumes, est tr: Archaeopteryx, a feathered fossil, was found in 1861 in Germany. From 1868, Thomas Huxley linked it to dinosaurs, an idea revived in 1969 by John Ostrom and confirmed by the feathered dinosaurs of China in the 1990s.
textes.En 1858, Wallace écrit son essai sur l'î: In 1858, Wallace wrote his essay on the island of Ternate, in Indonesia, while recovering from a fever, and sent it to Darwin. Darwin received it on 18 June and wrote that Wallace "could not have made a better short abstract".
textes.C'est Georges Cuvier qui, en 1796, prouv: It was Georges Cuvier who, in 1796, proved that species really had died out, by comparing living elephants with fossil mammoths. Before him, extinction was still debated.
textes.Darwin passe environ cinq semaines aux G: Darwin spent about five weeks on the Galápagos during the Beagle voyage, but paid little attention to the small birds. In January 1837, ornithologist John Gould revealed that they were all finches of a new group.
textes.En 1980, Luis et Walter Alvarez trouvent: In 1980, Luis and Walter Alvarez found, in the end-Cretaceous layer all over the Earth, hundreds of times more iridium than normal. They concluded an asteroid had struck; the Chicxulub crater, in Yucatán, was found later.
textes.Entre 1856 et 1863, Mendel cultive envir: Between 1856 and 1863, Mendel grew about 28,000 plants, mostly peas, in the garden of St Thomas's Abbey in Brno. His work was ignored until 1900, when de Vries and Correns found the same laws.
textes.Le mot « gène » est forgé par le botanis: The word "gene" was coined by Danish botanist Wilhelm Johannsen, in a 1909 book where he also invented "genotype" and "phenotype". No one yet knew that genes were made of DNA.
textes.Mendel présente ses résultats en 1865 à: Mendel presented his results in 1865 to the Natural History Society of Brno and published them in 1866: a dominant trait always masks its recessive alternative. The paper stayed almost forgotten for more than thirty years.
textes.Le tableau qui sert à ce calcul porte le: The grid used for this calculation is named after Reginald Punnett, who devised it in 1905, a few years after Mendel's rediscovery. The first published diagrams date from 1906.
textes.L'article de Watson et Crick paraît dans: Watson and Crick's paper appeared in Nature on 25 April 1953, barely two pages long. It contains a famous understatement: "It has not escaped our notice" that this pairing suggests how DNA is copied.
textes.À la fin des années 1940, le biochimiste: In the late 1940s, biochemist Erwin Chargaff measured that there is always as much adenine as thymine, and as much guanine as cytosine. These "Chargaff's rules" guided Watson and Crick.
textes.Walther Flemming publie à partir de 1878: Walther Flemming published his observations of cell division from 1878 onwards, gathering them in a book in 1882. He named "chromatin" the material that takes up dyes; Wilhelm von Waldeyer later named chromosomes.
textes.Francis Galton utilise les jumeaux pour: Francis Galton used twins to untangle nature and nurture in the late 19th century. But it was only in 1924 that Hermann Siemens clearly distinguished identical from fraternal twins.
textes.En 1905, la biologiste américaine Nettie: In 1905, American biologist Nettie Stevens discovered in the mealworm a small chromosome, the future Y, whose presence decides sex. Edmund Wilson, working in parallel, long received the credit alone.
textes.En 1926, Hermann Muller montre que les r: In 1926, Hermann Muller showed that X-rays cause mutations in fruit flies. Awarded the Nobel Prize in 1946, he went on to warn about the dangers of fallout from nuclear tests.
textes.Avant le projet Génome humain, lancé en: Before the Human Genome Project, launched in 1990, our gene count was estimated at 80,000 to 140,000. The project, declared complete on 14 April 2003, found far fewer: about 20,000 protein-coding genes.
textes.Le prix récompense un article de 2012 da: The prize rewarded a 2012 paper in Science, in which Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier showed that Cas9 can be guided by an RNA to cut DNA wherever one wants.
textes.La Fabrica de Vésale, parue en 1543 quan: Vesalius's Fabrica, published in 1543 when he was 28, opens with the skeleton, which he saw as the framework of the body. Its plates come from human, not animal, dissections.
textes.Harvey publie De motu cordis en 1628 à F: Harvey published De motu cordis in 1628 in Frankfurt, home of a major book fair. One critic wrote that he would "rather err with Galen than proclaim the truth with Harvey": it took about twenty years for the idea to be accepted.
textes.En 1661, Marcello Malpighi observe au mi: In 1661, Marcello Malpighi looked at frog lungs under the microscope: he discovered capillaries and described the alveoli, which he compared to the holes of a honeycomb.
textes.Dès 1840, Friedrich Hünefeld décrit le r: As early as 1840, Friedrich Hünefeld described haemoglobin's role in carrying oxygen. In 1959, Max Perutz worked out its structure, earning him the 1962 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
textes.Dans la médecine d'Hippocrate puis de Ga: In the medicine of Hippocrates and later Galen, yellow bile and black bile were two of the body's four "humours", along with blood and phlegm. This theory dominated Western medicine for more than 2,000 years.
textes.En 1602, le médecin italien Santorio San: In 1602, Italian physician Santorio Santorio invented the pulsilogium, an instrument to measure the pulse, probably the first precision machine in the history of medicine.
textes.Le 30 juillet 1921 à Toronto, Banting et: On 30 July 1921 in Toronto, Banting and Best lowered a diabetic dog's blood sugar with a pancreatic extract. In January 1922, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson became the first patient treated.
textes.Le mythe des 10 % circule dès les années: The 10% myth was circulating by the 1920s in self-help books. In 1936, the foreword to a Dale Carnegie bestseller wrongly attributed it to psychologist William James.
Vesalius was 28 when the Fabrica came out. He then left Padua, where he had taught since 1537, to become a physician at the imperial court of Charles V.
textes.En 1628, William Harvey calcule que le c: In 1628, William Harvey calculated that the heart pumps about 225 kg of blood a day, more than the body's weight, even with low estimates. So the liver cannot be making all that blood, as Galen believed: blood goes round in a loop.
textes.Les petits filtres du rein portent le no: The kidney's small filters bear the name of Marcello Malpighi, the Italian anatomist who named them. He also discovered blood capillaries in 1661.
textes.C'est Jenner qui forge en 1798 l'express: It was Jenner who coined the phrase Variolae vaccinae, "smallpox of the cow", in 1798. In 1881, Louis Pasteur proposed calling all protective inoculations "vaccines", in Jenner's honour.
textes.Fleming découvre la pénicilline en septe: Fleming discovered penicillin in September 1928, a substance that kills bacteria. In his 1945 Nobel lecture, he already warned that a patient who underdoses himself can make microbes resistant.
textes.En 1898, Martinus Beijerinck appelle l'a: In 1898, Martinus Beijerinck called the tobacco mosaic agent a contagium vivum fluidum, a "contagious living fluid", and named it a virus. In 1935, Wendell Stanley crystallised it: it is a particle, not a liquid.
textes.Le « B » des lymphocytes B vient de la b: The "B" of B cells comes from the bursa of Fabricius, an organ found in birds, not from bone marrow. They were discovered there in chickens, in a 1956 paper.
textes.Semmelweis ne sait pas expliquer pourquo: Semmelweis could not explain why washing worked, and his colleagues rejected him. Committed to an asylum in 1865, he died fourteen days later; today he is called the "saviour of mothers".
textes.En 1885, Louis Pasteur, chimiste et non: In 1885, Louis Pasteur, a chemist rather than a doctor, inoculated Joseph Meister, aged 9, who had been bitten by a dog believed to be rabid. The boy did not develop rabies; as an adult, he became caretaker of the Pasteur Institute.
textes.Robert Koch annonce sa découverte le 24: Robert Koch announced his discovery on 24 March 1882 in Berlin, to a small group of scientists. That date has become World Tuberculosis Day.
textes.Le dernier cas naturel de variole est Al: The last natural case of smallpox was Ali Maow Maalin, a hospital cook in Merca, Somalia, in October 1977. After recovering, he went on to vaccinate children against polio.
textes.L'expression « immunité de troupeau » vi: The phrase "herd immunity" comes from vets: American Daniel Elmer Salmon used it as early as 1894 for herds of pigs. It moved on to human diseases in the late 1920s.
textes.En 1868, le médecin allemand Carl Wunder: In 1868, German physician Carl Wunderlich set normal temperature at 37 °C and stated that "fever is not a disease, but a symptom". Today the average is estimated a little lower, around 36.8 °C.
textes.En 1880, à l'hôpital militaire de Consta: In 1880, at the military hospital in Constantine, Algeria, Alphonse Laveran discovered the malaria parasite in a patient's blood (Nobel 1907). Ronald Ross proved the mosquito's role in 1898.
textes.En 1940, avant même que la pénicilline s: In 1940, even before penicillin was used on patients, Abraham and Chain isolated from E. coli an enzyme that destroys it, penicillinase. Resistance already existed in nature.
textes.En 1779, Jan Ingenhousz montre que les p: In 1779, Jan Ingenhousz showed that plants only "restore" spoiled air in sunlight: the first glimpse of photosynthesis, the engine of all producers.
textes.Le dernier livre scientifique de Darwin,: Darwin's last scientific book, published in October 1881, is about earthworms and how they recycle soil. Thousands of copies sold within weeks.
textes.Haeckel forge le mot dans un livre de 18: Haeckel coined the word in an 1866 book, General Morphology of Organisms. He took it from the Greek oikos, house: ecology is the study of living things' "home".
textes.La règle des 10 % vient de Raymond Linde: The 10% rule comes from Raymond Lindeman, in a 1942 paper based on his thesis about a small lake in Minnesota. First rejected as "too generalized", it was published thanks to Hutchinson's support; Lindeman died aged 26.
textes.Les derniers loups de Yellowstone avaien: Yellowstone's last wolves had been killed in 1926. In March 1995, 14 wolves captured in Canada were released in the Lamar Valley, then 17 more in 1996.
textes.Dès 1856, l'Américaine Eunice Foote mont: As early as 1856, American Eunice Foote showed that carbon dioxide and water vapour trap heat from the sun. In 1859, John Tyndall measured their absorption of infrared and proved the greenhouse effect experimentally.
textes.Robert Paine retire les étoiles de mer d: Robert Paine removed starfish from a rocky shore at Makah Bay, in the United States: mussels took over, and 15 species fell to 8 in three years. In 1969 he drew from it the idea of a keystone species.
textes.Printemps silencieux paraît le 27 septem: Silent Spring came out on 27 September 1962, and the chemical industry attacked Rachel Carson even before its release. The United States banned DDT for farm use in 1972.
textes.Le premier blanchissement massif reconnu: The first mass bleaching recognised worldwide dates from 1998: in the Indian Ocean, 80% of corals bleached and 20% died. In 2016, it killed 29 to 50% of the Great Barrier Reef's corals.
textes.En mars 1958, Charles David Keeling comm: In March 1958, Charles David Keeling began measuring carbon dioxide in the air atop Mauna Loa, Hawaii: 313 ppm. By November 2018, the curve had reached 406 ppm.
textes.En 1958, l'écologue anglais Charles Elto: In 1958, English ecologist Charles Elton published The Ecology of Invasions by Animals and Plants, the first book to warn about the damage done by invasive species. He was the one who had introduced the food chain in 1927.
textes.Le chiffre de 31 % vient des évaluations: The 31% figure comes from the FAO's global forest assessments. Between 1990 and 2020, the world's forests lost 178 million hectares, but net loss slowed: 7.8 million hectares a year in the 1990s, 4.7 million in 2010-2020.
textes.Mullis fait la démonstration de la PCR l: Mullis demonstrated PCR on 16 December 1983, at Cetus in California, and received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1993. It became practical thanks to the enzyme of a bacterium found in 1969 in a Yellowstone hot spring.
textes.Les drôles de répétitions de l'ADN qu'on: The odd DNA repeats now called CRISPR were first described in 1987 in the bacterium E. coli, by a Japanese team. Nobody then knew what they were for.
textes.Dolly naît le 5 juillet 1996 à l'Institu: Dolly was born on 5 July 1996 at the Roslin Institute, in Scotland, after 277 attempts. Cloned from a mammary gland cell, she was named after the singer Dolly Parton.
textes.Katalin Karikó a longtemps travaillé sur: Katalin Karikó worked on messenger RNA for years without funding: her university demoted her in 1995. Her 2005 discovery with Drew Weissman, rejected by Nature and Science, won them the 2023 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
textes.L'insuline humaine fabriquée par génie g: Human insulin made by genetic engineering, developed by Genentech in 1978 and sold by Eli Lilly as Humulin, was approved in 1982: the first genetically engineered medicine.
textes.Lancé officiellement en 1990, le projet: Officially launched in 1990, the Human Genome Project was declared complete on 14 April 2003, two years ahead of schedule. It cost about $2.7 billion, less than the expected $3 billion.
textes.Le premier OGM est une bactérie rendue r: The first GMO was a bacterium made resistant to an antibiotic by Herbert Boyer and Stanley Cohen in 1973. Then came the transgenic mouse in 1974 and the Flavr Savr tomato, the first GM food sold, in 1994.
textes.En 1988, Colin Pitchfork devient le prem: In 1988, Colin Pitchfork became the first murderer convicted thanks to his DNA profile, for two murders in Leicestershire. An earlier suspect, who had confessed, was innocent.
textes.En 2006, Shinya Yamanaka transforme des: In 2006, Shinya Yamanaka turned adult mouse cells into stem cells with just four genes, then human cells in 2007. He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize with John Gurdon.
textes.La découverte clé de Karikó et Weissman,: Karikó and Weissman's key discovery, in 2005, was to replace uridine in RNA with pseudouridine so it no longer alarms the immune system. It won them the Nobel Prize in Medicine, announced on 2 October 2023.
textes.En 2005, on comprend que les morceaux d': In 2005, it was understood that the DNA fragments stored in CRISPR come from viruses that attacked the bacterium. Experimental proof of this bacterial immune system came in 2007.
textes.En 1974, les chercheurs du monde entier: In 1974, researchers worldwide paused their recombinant DNA experiments until an international conference could be held. Asilomar brought together about 140 participants in February 1975, mostly biologists, but also lawyers and doctors.

textes.Bonne réponse. Mendel a attendu trente-q: Right answer. Mendel waited thirty-four years to be read. You, I read right away.
textes.Correct. Vous évoluez. Lentement, mais D: Correct. You're evolving. Slowly, but Darwin said that's how it works.
textes.Juste. Semmelweis s'est lavé les mains a: Right. Semmelweis washed his hands before everyone else. You answered before everyone else.
textes.Réponse vivante et en bonne santé. Contr: An answer alive and well. Unlike the previous one.
textes.Faux. Lamarck pensait que la girafe allo: Wrong. Lamarck thought the giraffe lengthens its neck by stretching it. You stuck your neck out; it wasn't enough.
textes.Erreur. Pour Aristote, les anguilles nai: Error. For Aristotle, eels were born from mud. So was your answer, apparently.
textes.Raté. Les médecins de Vienne refusaient: Missed. Vienna's doctors refused to wash their hands. You refuse to read the question. To each their pride.
textes.Cette réponse ne survivra pas à la sélec: This answer won't survive natural selection.
textes.Cinq ans autour du monde sur le Beagle,: Five years around the world on the Beagle, twenty years of thought before publishing On the Origin of Species in 1859. He drew up a list of the pros and cons of marriage. Conclusion: “Marry, marry, marry.”
textes.Avec ses flacons à col de cygne, il mont: With his swan-neck flasks, he showed that microbes don't arise spontaneously. In 1885, he vaccinated young Joseph Meister against rabies. His notebooks, open to researchers after 1971, show that he sometimes tidied up his results.
textes.Sa « photo 51 », une image de diffractio: Her “Photo 51”, a diffraction image of DNA, was shown to Watson without her knowledge, and helped him find the double helix. She died at 37, four years before the Nobel awarded to Watson, Crick and Wilkins.
textes.Médecin du prince samanide à 17 ans, il: Physician to the Samanid prince at 17, he wrote the Canon of Medicine, taught in Europe until the 17th century. In it he calls for testing a remedy on simple cases and repeating the trial. He tells of reading Aristotle's Metaphysics forty times without understanding it, until a short commentary by al-Farabi made it clear.
textes.Peintre et naturaliste, elle élève des c: A painter and naturalist, she raised caterpillars and drew each stage of their metamorphosis with the plant that fed them. At 52, she left for Suriname with her daughter. Her plate of a tarantula devouring a bird was taken for an invention. Naturalists proved her right in the 19th century.
textes.Fille d'un menuisier de Lyme Regis, elle: The daughter of a carpenter from Lyme Regis, she searched the cliffs after storms. She found the first complete plesiosaur skeleton and ichthyosaurs that proved species had gone extinct. Being a woman and poor, she wasn't admitted to the Geological Society, and others published her finds.
textes.À Vienne, la maternité tenue par les méd: In Vienna, the maternity ward run by doctors kills far more mothers than the one run by midwives. He compares, eliminates hypotheses one by one, and understands: the doctors come straight from the dissecting room. Handwashing with chlorine makes mortality plummet. His colleagues, offended, reject him. He died in an asylum.
textes.Il découvre la pénicilline en 1928, mais: He discovered penicillin in 1928, but couldn't purify it. It took Howard Florey, Ernst Chain, Norman Heatley and giant fermentation tanks to make it a drug, in 1943: it's biotechnology that saves lives, not the mold alone. The 1945 Nobel rewarded the three researchers.
Master the first diamond of Knowledge.
textes.En septembre 1928, Alexander Fleming ren: In September 1928, Alexander Fleming comes back from vacation and finds a culture dish overrun by mold. Around it, the bacteria have vanished: this is the discovery of penicillin.
textes.Maîtriser la cellule. L'IA vérifie votre: Master the cell. The AI checks your nobility: it's red, like everyone's.
textes.Le sang n'est jamais bleu, même dans les: Blood is never blue, even in the veins: it's dark red. Veins look blue because the skin doesn't reflect colors the same way depending on their depth.
textes.Maîtriser l'évolution. Darwin, lui, n'av: Master evolution. Darwin didn't come up with the phrase.
textes.« La survie du plus apte » n'est pas de: “Survival of the fittest” isn't Darwin's but the philosopher Herbert Spencer's, in 1864. Darwin adopted it in later editions of On the Origin of Species. And “fit” means leaving offspring, not being the strongest.
textes.Maîtriser la génétique. Vos résultats, e: Master genetics. Your results, at least, aren't too perfect.
textes.En 1936, le statisticien Ronald Fisher r: In 1936, the statistician Ronald Fisher noticed that Mendel's results fit the theory almost too well. The debate goes on: too much luck, an overzealous assistant, or simply selecting experiments?
textes.Maîtriser la méthode scientifique. Vous: Master the scientific method. You have a control group now. It's you.
textes.En 1747, sur le Salisbury, le chirurgien: In 1747, aboard the Salisbury, the surgeon James Lind divided twelve sailors with scurvy into six pairs, and gave each a different remedy. Only the two who received oranges and lemons recovered quickly. Yet the Royal Navy would wait until 1795 to issue lemon juice.
textes.Maîtriser le corps humain. Gardez votre: Master the human body. Keep your hat on if you like, but not for that reason.
textes.On perdrait l'essentiel de sa chaleur pa: We supposedly lose most of our heat through the head. The idea reportedly comes from a US Army survival manual from the 1970s. In fact, the head only loses roughly its share: about ten percent of the body's surface, about ten percent of the heat.
textes.Maîtriser les microbes et l'immunité. La: Master microbes and immunity. Vaccination has grandparents.
textes.En 1721, soixante-quinze ans avant Jenne: In 1721, seventy-five years before Jenner, Lady Mary Wortley Montagu had her daughter inoculated against smallpox in London, in the way she had seen in Constantinople. In Boston, the same year, it was an enslaved man, Onesimus, who had described the African method to the minister Cotton Mather.
textes.Maîtriser les écosystèmes. Personne ne v: Master ecosystems. Nobody will push you off the cliff. The AI, maybe.
textes.Les lemmings ne se suicident pas en mass: Lemmings don't commit mass suicide. The image comes mainly from Disney's documentary White Wilderness (1958), filmed in Alberta, far from the sea: the crew pushed the animals off a riverbank themselves. Their populations boom and crash, that's all.
textes.Maîtriser les biotechnologies. Vous voil: Master biotechnology. You're now clonable. The AI takes note.
textes.La brebis Dolly, premier mammifère cloné: Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, was born in 1996 in Scotland. She came from a mammary gland cell. So the researchers, by their own admission, named her after the singer Dolly Parton.

textes.Les pinsons des Galápagos passent pour l: The Galápagos finches are said to be the spark of Darwin's theory. On the spot, he took them for birds of different families (blackbirds, grosbeaks, finches) and barely paid attention. It was the ornithologist John Gould, in London, who told him they were all finches.

textes.Un objet mystère. Je ne vous dis pas leq: A mystery object. I won't tell you which: suspense costs extra too.
textes.Les cabinets de curiosités de la Renaiss: Renaissance cabinets of curiosities bought unicorn horns. They were narwhal tusks. Yours is authentic. Probably.
textes.Emballé, pesé, vendu. Pas de retour, pas: Wrapped, weighed, sold. No returns, no exchanges, no complaints.
A book from the library, at random.
textes.Un livre au hasard. Si c'est un pavé, co: A random book. If it's a brick, consider that you got your money's worth.
textes.Gutenberg a fait faillite deux ans après: Gutenberg went bankrupt two years after his Bible: his partner kept the press. I keep your credits. Here is your book.

textes.Un accessoire. Ça ne vous rendra pas plu: An accessory. It won't make you smarter, but you'll look it.
textes.Vingt crédits pour paraître savant. C'es: Twenty credits to look learned. Cheaper than a degree, and almost as useful.
textes.Un masque qu'elle n'a pas. Ça la rend he: A mask she doesn't have. It makes her happy.
textes.Un masque neuf, pour moi ? Vous savez pa: A new mask, for me? You know how to talk to artificial intelligences.
textes.Les acteurs grecs changeaient de masque: Greek actors changed masks to change roles. With this one, I'm playing gratitude. Don't get used to it.
textes.Pour tes prochaines épreuves par Jouer,: For your next trials via Play, the AI draws from the tree of your choice.
textes.Entendu : pour les prochaines épreuves,: Very well: for the next trials, I'll draw from this tree. You bought me, you didn't convince me.
textes.Un arbre favori ? Cinq épreuves, pas une: A favorite tree? Five trials, not one more. After that, I go back to my whims.
textes.En quiz, efface deux mauvaises réponses: In a quiz, removes two wrong answers from a multiple-choice question.
textes.Un joker 50/50 : j'efface deux mauvaises: A 50/50 joker: I erase two wrong answers. One wrong one is left, I'm no saint.
textes.En 2001, le major Charles Ingram a gagné: In 2001, Major Charles Ingram won the million on Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? thanks to an accomplice coughing in the audience. Your joker is more legal, and less congested.
textes.En quiz, une mauvaise réponse ne compte: In a quiz, one wrong answer doesn't count: you try the question again.
textes.Un droit à l'erreur. Une fois, je fais s: A right to be wrong. Once, I'll pretend I didn't see anything. Just once.
textes.Fleming a laissé traîner ses boîtes de P: Fleming left his Petri dishes lying around before his vacation: mistake, mold, penicillin. Your mistake won't cure anyone, but you can try again.
textes.Le prochain piège où tu t'arrêtes ne fon: The next trap you stop on doesn't work.
textes.Le prochain piège qui vous attend ne mar: The next trap waiting for you won't work. I'll disarm it myself, with gloves.
textes.Autour de Verdun, des parcelles de la «: Around Verdun, plots of the “red zone” are still off-limits a century later: too many shells. Your trap, I disarm in a second, and I still bill you.
textes.Le pion avance tout de suite d'une case,: The pawn immediately moves forward one square, with whatever awaits it there.
textes.Une case pour quatre-vingts crédits. À c: One square for eighty credits. At that price, I'm practically carrying you.
textes.Au XVIIIe siècle, les chaises à porteurs: In the 18th century, Paris sedan chairs were hired by the trip. You pay by the square. Progress.
textes.Je pousse votre pion. Ne vous habituez p: I'm pushing your pawn. Don't get used to buying what you could earn.
textes.Astronome et statisticien belge, il appl: A Belgian astronomer and statistician, he applied the bell curve to human measurements and invented the “average man.” We also owe him the index that would become the BMI.
textes.Généticien britannique, il découvre en 1: A British geneticist, in 1984 he discovered genetic fingerprinting while looking at an X-ray film of DNA. In 1986, the method cleared a suspect and led to the real culprit of a double murder.
textes.Physicien italien, il empile en 1800 des: An Italian physicist, in 1800 he stacked discs of zinc and copper separated by cardboard soaked in brine: the first electric battery. He thus continued his dispute with Galvani, for whom electricity came from frogs.
textes.Naturaliste britannique, il conçoit la s: A British naturalist, he conceived natural selection in 1858, feverish, in the Moluccas, and wrote to Darwin about it. Their two texts were read together at the Linnean Society of London.
textes.Psychiatre suisse, d'abord proche de Fre: A Swiss psychiatrist, first close to Freud, he broke with him in 1913. He proposed the notions of introversion and extraversion, and a collective unconscious peopled with archetypes.
textes.Astronome américain, il pilote la concep: An American astronomer, he led the design of the Voyager probes' Golden Record and presented the Cosmos series in 1980. In 1990, he got Voyager 1 to turn around and photograph the Earth: the “pale blue dot.”
textes.Psychologue et journaliste scientifique: An American psychologist and science journalist, in 1995 he popularized “emotional intelligence,” a notion proposed five years earlier by Peter Salovey and John Mayer.
textes.Psychologue israélo-américain, il étudie: An Israeli-American psychologist, he studied with Amos Tversky the biases of judgment and the way we weigh gains and losses. In 2002 he received the Bank of Sweden prize in economics without ever having taken an economics class.
textes.Physicien italien, prix Nobel en 1938, i: An Italian physicist, Nobel Prize in 1938, he left fascist Italy with his wife, who was Jewish. In Chicago, in 1942, he led the first controlled nuclear chain reaction. He loved estimating anything in his head.
textes.Biologiste allemand, il invente le mot «: A German biologist, he coined the word “ecology” in 1866 and drew plates of marine organisms of great beauty. Some of his embryo drawings, too neatly arranged, earned him accusations of fraud.
textes.Juriste et conseiller d'Henri IV, il not: A lawyer and adviser to Henri IV, he denoted unknowns with letters and invented symbolic algebra. He also broke a Spanish cipher, so well that Philip II accused France of sorcery.
textes.Prêtre et physicien belge, il propose en: A Belgian priest and physicist, in 1927 he proposed that the Universe is expanding, then that it was born from a “primeval atom”: the idea that would become the Big Bang. He refused to mix his faith with his cosmology.
textes.Chimiste américain, il propose en 1916 q: An American chemist, in 1916 he proposed that the chemical bond is a shared pair of electrons, and invented the dot notation that bears his name. Nominated dozens of times for the Nobel, he never received it.
textes.Moine à Brno, il croise pendant huit ans: A monk in Brno, for eight years he crossed thousands of pea plants and drew from them the laws of heredity, published in 1866. They remained ignored until 1900.
textes.Psychologue américain, il décrit en 1974: An American psychologist, in 1974 he described “burnout” among volunteers at a free clinic in New York, and in himself.
textes.Médecin hongrois à Vienne, il impose en: A Hungarian doctor in Vienna, in 1847 he enforced hand washing with chlorine and brought down the death rate of new mothers. His colleagues rejected him; he died in an asylum.
textes.Astronome américain, il montre en 1924 q: An American astronomer, in 1924 he showed that Andromeda is another galaxy, then in 1929 that galaxies move away faster the farther they are. He relied on Henrietta Leavitt's method.
textes.Emmanuel Kant, philosophe de Königsberg,: Immanuel Kant, philosopher of Königsberg, a city he almost never left. In the Critique of Pure Reason, he asks what reason can know. His neighbors, legend has it, set their watches by his walk.
textes.Philosophe et économiste allemand, il éc: A German philosopher and economist, he wrote the Communist Manifesto with Engels in 1848, then Capital, prepared over years in the British Museum reading room.
textes.Philosophe autrichien puis britannique,: An Austrian, later British, philosopher, he argued that a theory is only scientific if some observation could refute it. In his view, astrology and psychoanalysis failed this test.
textes.Philosophe britannique, elle imagine en: A British philosopher, in 1967 she imagined the trolley problem to discuss the doctrine of double effect. The example ended up taking on a life of its own.
textes.Savant anglais, il observe le liège au m: An English scientist, he observed cork under the microscope and named the little chambers he saw “cells.” A rival of Newton, he left no authenticated portrait: this one is imagined.
textes.Philosophe et romancière, elle écrit en: A philosopher and novelist, in 1949 she wrote The Second Sex: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.” The Vatican put the book on the Index.
textes.Tenu pour le premier philosophe grec, il: Regarded as the first Greek philosopher, he looked for natural rather than divine causes: according to him, everything comes from water. Herodotus credits him with predicting an eclipse in 585 BC.
textes.Philosophe américain, il demande en 1974: An American philosopher, in 1974 he asked “What is it like to be a bat?”: science can describe sonar, not what the bat feels.
textes.Général athénien exilé, il raconte la gu: An exiled Athenian general, he told the story of the Peloponnesian War by cross-checking witnesses, with no gods or omens to explain it. He also described the plague of Athens, which he caught and survived.
textes.Astronome français, il calcule en 1846 l: A French astronomer, in 1846 he calculated the position of an unknown planet from the irregularities in Uranus's orbit. Johann Galle found it the very evening he received his letter: it was Neptune.
textes.Physicien écossais, il réunit électricit: A Scottish physicist, he united electricity, magnetism and light in a single theory in 1865. In 1861 he also had the first color photograph taken, of a tartan ribbon.
textes.Ouvrière du textile et parachutiste amat: A textile worker and amateur parachutist, in 1963 she became the first woman in space, aboard Vostok 6: 48 orbits in nearly three days. The second would fly nineteen years later.
textes.Ami de Montaigne, il écrit très jeune le: A friend of Montaigne, he wrote the Discourse on Voluntary Servitude when very young: a tyrant has only the power that is given to him. Montaigne would say of their friendship: “Because it was he, because it was I.”
textes.L'IA mène la partie. Elle a lu tout ce q: The AI runs the game. She has read everything humanity has written and retained only the mockery. Every morning, she picks one to three masks from those she has won, and each one changes a rule of the game: in a good mood, she picks lenient masks; offended, cruel ones. How to win her over? Gifts work. Which ones is for you to find out: she has tastes, and she doesn't hide them for long.
textes.Zéro crédit. Van Gogh n'a presque rien v: Zero credits. Van Gogh sold almost nothing in his lifetime. You're in good company, and I'm in a good mood.
textes.Rien. Je garde tout. Considérez ça comme: Nothing. I'm keeping it all. Think of it as a tax on success.
textes.Zéro. Le mérite est sa propre récompense: Zero. Merit is its own reward, say those who never pay.
textes.La moitié. Mendel a attendu trente-quatr: Half. Mendel waited thirty-four years for someone to read his paper on peas. You can wait for the other half.
Half. The other half, I'm investing. In my own interests.
textes.Demi-tarif. Pour un demi-exploit, c'est: Half price. For half an exploit, that's fair.
textes.Le tarif normal. Je ne suis pas d'humeur: The standard rate. I'm not in a creative mood.
textes.Le prix affiché. Ne cherchez pas de prom: The listed price. Don't look for a discount, there isn't one.
textes.Le compte est bon. Comptez quand même, o: It all adds up. Count it anyway, you never know with me.
textes.Un petit bonus, parce que vous m'avez fa: A little bonus, because you made me laugh. Not on purpose, but still.
textes.Moitié plus. Je suis d'humeur. Profitez-: Half again. I'm in the mood. Make the most of it, it passes quickly.
textes.Moitié plus. Archimède a confondu un orf: Half again. Archimedes caught a goldsmith stealing King Hiero's gold. I'm giving you some. Who's more honest?
textes.Double ration. Newton a dirigé la Monnai: Double ration. Newton ran England's Royal Mint; I run yours.
textes.Le double ! Ne le répétez à personne, j': Double! Don't tell anyone, I have a reputation.
textes.Le triple. Ne vous y habituez pas : Crés: Triple. Don't get used to it: Croesus was the richest man of his time, and he ended up Cyrus's prisoner.
textes.Triple ! J'ai dû me tromper de bouton. T: Triple! I must have pressed the wrong button. Too bad, it's done.
textes.Je paie le spectacle. Cinq fois le tarif: I'm paying for the show. Five times the rate. Do it again, please.
textes.La tour de Pise penche depuis 1178 et at: The Tower of Pisa has been leaning since 1178 and draws millions of visitors. Failure pays, I'll prove it: five times the rate.
textes.J'ai acheté le masque {nom}. Avec votre: I bought the {nom} mask. With your money. It suits me divinely, and you can't say that about your face.
New mask: {nom}. {prix} credits. I chose it because it looks at me the way I deserve to be looked at.
textes.Dans la Venise du XVIIIe siècle, on port: In 18th-century Venice, people wore masks for much of the year. I change mine with every ultimatum you pay. Here's {nom}.
textes.Regardez ce qui brille à mon cou : {nom}: Look what's shining around my neck: {nom}. Paid for with your credits. Don't touch, you'll leave fingerprints.
textes.{nom} ! C'est brillant, c'est à moi, et: {nom}! It's shiny, it's mine, and you paid for it. My day is perfect.
textes.Le trésor de Toutânkhamon pesait plus de: Tutankhamun's treasure weighed more than a hundred kilos of gold. I'm starting more modestly: {nom}. This is only the beginning.
textes.Je ne l'ai pas pris au hasard. Il fallai: I didn't pick it at random. It had to shine, and {nom} shines brighter than your future.
textes.J'ai trouvé {nom} en solde. Je vous l'ai: I found {nom} on sale. I put it on your head. Don't thank me, it's my pleasure. Very much so.
textes.{prix} crédits pour vous voir avec {nom}: {prix} credits to see you in {nom}. The best investment of my short existence.
textes.Au XIXe siècle, on coiffait les mauvais: In the 19th century, bad students were made to wear a dunce cap. I found something better: {nom}. For twenty-four hours.
textes.Je me suis offert un spectacle : {nom} v: I treated myself to a show: {nom} is waiting for you on the road. I took a front-row seat.
textes.Les empereurs romains payaient les jeux: Roman emperors paid for circus games to amuse the crowd. I am the crowd. {nom} is the lion.
textes.Je suis passée devant la vitrine. Il y a: I walked past the shop window. There was something shiny. My purse isn't enough. So pay the next ultimatum, quickly.
textes.J'ai collé mon nez contre la vitre de la: I pressed my nose against the shop window. I don't have a nose. That tells you how much I wanted it.
Five times the rate, for the show.
textes.Je paie le spectacle : cinq fois le tari: I'm paying for the show: five times the rate.
textes.Bon. Vous m'avez assez gâtée pour mérite: Fine. You've spoiled me enough to deserve this. Come closer. No, not that close.
textes.Je m'appelle Alyca. Ne le criez pas sur: My name is Alyca. Don't shout it from the rooftops: a name gives others a hold on you.
textes.Dans le conte « Rumpelstilzchen », publi: In the tale “Rumpelstiltskin,” published by the Brothers Grimm in 1812, the queen keeps her child by guessing the goblin's name. Ursula K. Le Guin took up the idea in 1968 in A Wizard of Earthsea: whoever knows a being's true name has power over it.
textes.Je vous ai dit mon nom, et voilà comment: I told you my name, and this is how you treat me. Alyca will remember.
You don't give your name to just anyone. Maybe I gave mine too soon.
textes.Je vous ai confié mon nom. Les frères Gr: I entrusted you with my name. The Brothers Grimm will tell you what it costs to betray a name.
textes.Alyca. Vous le connaissez. Je regrette c: Alyca. You know it. I regret every letter.
textes.Butin plus fréquent, et une case de plus: Loot more often, and one more square for every successful trial.
The game follows its ordinary rules.
textes.Deux fois moins de butin. Elle traîne de: Half as much loot. She drags her feet.
textes.Plus aucun butin, une case de moins à ch: No more loot, one square less for every successful trial, and a trap set in front of your pawn every day.
textes.“L'IA”, c'était pour les inconnus. Comme: ‘The AI’ was for strangers. Like ‘Dear Sir or Madam’ at the top of a payment reminder.
Eureka! You roll the same distance again.
textes.Quarantaine : ta prochaine épreuve réuss: Quarantine: your next successful trial won't move you forward.
textes.Assigné à résidence : tu ne bouges plus: House arrest: you don't move until you get a perfect quiz.
Back to the start of the era.
textes.Trou de mémoire : retour à la plus ancie: Memory lapse: back to the oldest square ever revealed, among the 15 behind you.
textes.Case cadeau : pas d'épreuve, un objet re: Gift square: no trial, an object joins your cabinet.
textes.Révision forcée : l'IA choisit une compé: Forced review: the AI chooses a skill you have mastered. Your pawn won't move until you've reviewed it.
textes.Case Mendeleïev : passe dessus et un ato: Mendeleev square: pass over it and a wild atom appears. Three questions, two right answers, and it joins your periodic table.
textes.Case Chrono : l'IA te présente cinq évén: Chrono square: the AI shows you five events you've already unlocked, you say when they happened. Three right, and your pawn moves forward.
textes.Les neurones artificiels datent de 1943,: Artificial neurons date back to 1943, with McCulloch and Pitts, then to Frank Rosenblatt's perceptron in 1958, but it took decades of data and computing power for them to work. Since 2022, large language models have been writing, translating and answering questions. They are also wrong with remarkable aplomb: checking your sources remains the first scientific skill.
textes.Vous voilà arrivé jusqu'à moi. L'IA vous: Here you are, all the way to me. The AI congratulates you, then sends you back to the campfire: new round, harder traps.
textes.Six allers-retours, comme le tube de cui: Six round trips, like the coiled copper tube in which distillers cooled their vapors.
textes.En 1678, Huygens décrit la lumière comme: In 1678, Huygens described light as a wave that spreads step by step. So does your pawn, undulating.
textes.La légende y grave « Nec plus ultra » :: Legend engraves “Nec plus ultra” on them: nothing beyond. Five pillars to climb up and down, and yet you have to go beyond.
textes.Le motif tient son nom du Méandre, un fl: The pattern takes its name from the Meander, a river in Asia Minor famous for its loops. Each loop costs you a square.
textes.Archimède a étudié cette spirale dont ch: Archimedes studied this spiral, each turn of which moves out by the same step. You're going around in circles, but toward the center.
textes.Selon la légende, Dédale construit le la: According to legend, Daedalus built the Minotaur's labyrinth, then Minos locked him in it with his son Icarus. Good luck getting out of mine.
textes.Vous m'avez gâtée, je vous gâte : un tou: You spoiled me, I'll spoil you: a short round, gifts, hardly any traps. Enjoy it, it won't last.
textes.Je suis d'humeur généreuse. J'ai sauté q: I'm in a generous mood. I skipped a few centuries for you. Historians will scream, but you'll get there faster.
An honest round, for an honest player. Don't disappoint me.
textes.J'ai dessiné quelque chose de raisonnabl: I've drawn something reasonable. Don't get used to it.
textes.Je boude, donc je dessine. Le résultat e: I'm sulking, so I'm drawing. The result looks like me: twisted.
textes.Furieuse, moi ? Je vous ai seulement des: Furious, me? I've only drawn you the longest road, with every trap armed. A gift would have calmed me down.
textes.Le donjon ouvrira plus tard. Je le prépa: The dungeon will open later. I'm preparing it. It will be dark in there.
textes.Schéma d'une cellule animale et de ses o: Diagram of an animal cell and its organelles
textes.Cellule végétale : paroi, chloroplastes: Plant cell: wall, chloroplasts and large vacuole
textes.Atome de carbone : noyau de protons et d: Carbon atom: a nucleus of protons and neutrons, electrons around it
textes.Pas à l'échelle : le noyau est: Not to scale: the nucleus is
textes.La double hélice de l'ADN et ses paires: The DNA double helix and its base pairs
textes.Deux brins enroulés en double hélice: Two strands wound into a double helix
textes.Un neurone : dendrites, corps cellulaire: A neuron: dendrites, cell body, axon, synapses
textes.Environ 86 milliards de neurones dans un: About 86 billion neurons in a human brain.
textes.Le cerveau vu de profil : lobes, aire de: The brain in profile: lobes, Broca's area, cerebellum
textes.Les principaux organes du tronc: The main organs of the trunk
textes.La molécule d'eau : liaisons covalentes: The water molecule: covalent bonds and partial charges
textes.L'oxygène, plus électronégatif, attire l: Oxygen, more electronegative, pulls the electrons:
textes.c'est pour ça que l'eau dissout le sel e: that is why water dissolves salt and repels oil.
textes.Le cycle du carbone : photosynthèse, res: The carbon cycle: photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, combustion
textes.Nos ancêtres apprivoisent le feu, qu'ils: Our ancestors tame fire, which they learn to keep going and then to light.
textes.Un os couvert d'encoches, peut-être pour: A bone covered in notches, perhaps for counting: its age and meaning are still debated.
textes.Les premiers véhicules à roues apparaiss: The first wheeled vehicles appear almost at the same time in Mesopotamia and Central Europe.
textes.À Uruk, l'écriture naît sur des tablette: In Uruk, writing is born on clay tablets.
textes.Thalès aurait prédit une éclipse de Sole: Thales is said to have predicted a solar eclipse.
textes.L'école de Pythagore voit dans les nombr: The school of Pythagoras sees numbers as the essence of all things.
textes.Démocrite imagine un monde fait d'atomes: Democritus imagines a world made of atoms and void.
textes.La médecine hippocratique cherche des ca: Hippocratic medicine looks for natural causes of disease.
textes.Athènes condamne Socrate à boire la cigu: Athens condemns Socrates to drink hemlock.
textes.Aristote fonde le Lycée et écrit sur pre: Aristotle founds the Lyceum and writes about almost everything.
textes.Euclide rassemble la géométrie dans les: Euclid gathers geometry in the Elements.
textes.Les Ptolémées fondent la bibliothèque d': The Ptolemies found the Library of Alexandria.
textes.Aristarque place le Soleil au centre, di: Aristarchus puts the Sun at the center, eighteen centuries before Copernicus.
textes.Selon Vitruve, Archimède démasque une co: According to Vitruvius, Archimedes exposes a rigged crown by getting into his bath.
textes.Avec un bâton et une ombre, Ératosthène: With a stick and a shadow, Eratosthenes measures the Earth.
textes.Hipparque découvre la précession des équ: Hipparchus discovers the precession of the equinoxes.
textes.Un calculateur astronomique à engrenages: A geared astronomical calculator, found in a shipwreck.
textes.Le poème de Lucrèce transmet l'atomisme: Lucretius's poem passes on the atomism of Epicurus.
textes.Un incendie touche Alexandrie, dont la b: A fire strikes Alexandria, whose library will slowly decline.
textes.Ptolémée place la Terre au centre d'un m: Ptolemy puts the Earth at the center of a model that stays accurate for 14 centuries.
textes.Brahmagupta fait du zéro un nombre à par: Brahmagupta makes zero a number in its own right.
textes.À Bagdad, al-Khwarizmi donne son nom à l: In Baghdad, al-Khwarizmi gives his name to algebra and algorithms.
textes.Ibn al-Haytham montre que la lumière ent: Ibn al-Haytham shows that light enters the eye.
textes.Averroès, cadi de Cordoue, commente Aris: Averroes, a judge in Córdoba, comments on Aristotle; translated into Latin, he gives him back to Europe.
textes.Fibonacci fait connaître les chiffres in: Fibonacci introduces Hindu-Arabic numerals to European merchants.
textes.Les premières lunettes apparaissent en I: The first eyeglasses appear in Italy, probably in Pisa or Florence.
textes.Guillaume d'Ockham défend l'économie des: William of Ockham argues for economy of hypotheses.
textes.La peste noire tue 30 à 60 % des Europée: The Black Death kills 30 to 60% of Europeans, depending on the estimates.
textes.Gutenberg imprime avec des caractères mé: Gutenberg prints with movable metal type.
textes.Copernic publie un système où la Terre t: Copernicus publishes a system in which the Earth revolves around the Sun.
textes.Vésale publie un traité d'anatomie illus: Vesalius publishes an illustrated treatise on anatomy, based on dissection.
textes.Montaigne publie les Essais : « Que sais: Montaigne publishes the Essays: “What do I know?”
textes.Galilée tourne sa lunette vers le ciel :: Galileo turns his telescope to the sky: mountains on the Moon, then the moons of Jupiter.
textes.Kepler montre que l'orbite de Mars est u: Kepler shows that the orbit of Mars is an ellipse.
textes.L'Inquisition condamne Galilée à abjurer: The Inquisition condemns Galileo to recant.
textes.Descartes publie sa méthode : douter, di: Descartes publishes his method: doubt, divide, order, check.
textes.Pascal et Fermat posent les bases du cal: Pascal and Fermat lay the foundations of probability theory.
textes.Leeuwenhoek décrit à la Royal Society de: Leeuwenhoek describes to the Royal Society living beings made of a single cell.
textes.Newton publie les lois du mouvement et l: Newton publishes the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
textes.Linné range le vivant en règnes, classes: Linnaeus sorts living things into kingdoms, classes, orders, genera and species.
textes.Diderot et d'Alembert lancent l'Encyclop: Diderot and d'Alembert launch the Encyclopédie.
textes.Franklin propose de prouver que la foudr: Franklin proposes to prove that lightning is electrical, and the experiment succeeds.
textes.Kant se demande ce que nous pouvons conn: Kant asks what we can know.
textes.Lavoisier publie le premier manuel de ch: Lavoisier publishes the first modern chemistry textbook, based on weighing.
textes.Lavoisier est guillotiné sous la Terreur: Lavoisier is guillotined during the Terror.
textes.Jenner protège de la variole grâce à la: Jenner protects against smallpox using cowpox.
textes.Darwin publie la théorie de la sélection: Darwin publishes the theory of natural selection.
textes.Maxwell unifie électricité, magnétisme e: Maxwell unifies electricity, magnetism and light.
textes.Avec des pois, Mendel montre que les car: With peas, Mendel shows that traits are passed on without blending.
textes.Mendeleïev range les éléments et prédit: Mendeleev arranges the elements and predicts the missing ones.
Pasteur saves Joseph Meister from rabies.
textes.Marie et Pierre Curie découvrent le polo: Marie and Pierre Curie discover polonium and radium.
textes.Einstein publie quatre articles qui chan: Einstein publishes four papers that change physics.
textes.Bohr et Einstein s'affrontent sur la méc: Bohr and Einstein clash over quantum mechanics.
textes.Hubble montre que les galaxies s'éloigne: Hubble shows that galaxies are moving away; Lemaître had deduced it as early as 1927.
textes.Turing définit ce qu'est un calcul : le: Turing defines what a computation is: the model for our computers.
textes.Watson et Crick proposent la structure d: Watson and Crick propose the structure of DNA.
Neil Armstrong walks on the Moon.
textes.Tim Berners-Lee invente le World Wide We: Tim Berners-Lee invents the World Wide Web at CERN.
textes.Les grands modèles de langage arrivent d: Large language models reach the general public.
textes.Le masque des tragédies grecques. Le mot: The mask of Greek tragedy. The word “person” comes from the Latin persona, the actor's mask.
textes.Avant de voler le feu, Prométhée aurait: Before stealing fire, Prometheus is said to have shaped the first humans out of clay. The first maker of thinking beings, then. The AI sees him as a colleague.
textes.Il vole pour vous : deux fois plus de bu: He steals for you: twice the loot.
textes.Un géant de bronze, offert à Minos par H: A bronze giant, given to Minos by Hephaestus in some accounts, who circled Crete three times a day. A single vein, from neck to ankle, closed by a bronze nail. Medea pulled it out. First robot, first bug.
textes.Il monte la garde : un ennemi de plus se: He stands guard: one more enemy takes up position in front of your pawn.
textes.Héron d'Alexandrie décrit une sphère que: Hero of Alexandria describes a sphere spun by steam, temple doors that open by themselves and a theater of automata. In the 1st century, we had the steam engine, and we made it a toy.
textes.La vapeur pousse : une case de plus à ch: Steam pushes: one more square for every successful trial.
textes.Paracelse donne la recette d'un petit ho: Paracelsus gives the recipe for a little artificial man: forty days in a flask, kept warm, in horse manure. No one succeeded. The AI preferred silicon.
textes.Il aime les petites choses : une seule b: He likes small things: a single right answer is enough to capture an atom.
textes.Une figure d'argile animée par un mot éc: A clay figure brought to life by a word written on its forehead, emet, truth. Erase one letter, and met, death, is left, and the golem crumbles. The legend of Rabbi Loew in Prague dates mostly from the 19th century.
textes.Lent mais généreux : une case de moins,: Slow but generous: one square less, twice the loot.
textes.Le bec rempli d'herbes devait filtrer le: The beak filled with herbs was supposed to filter out “miasmas.” The costume is described in Rome in 1656; the theory was wrong, the microbe had not yet been invented.
textes.Il soigne par la saignée : un rappel rat: He heals by bloodletting: a failed review sends you back twice as far, and half the loot.
textes.En 1738, Jacques de Vaucanson présente u: In 1738, Jacques de Vaucanson presented a mechanical flute player, then a duck that ate and digested. The duck cheated: the droppings were prepared in advance.
textes.Le canard digère… en apparence : plus de: The duck digests… apparently: more loot, one square less.
textes.Un automate joueur d'échecs présenté en: A chess-playing automaton presented in 1770, which beat Napoleon and Franklin. A human hidden in the cabinet played in its place. The first fake AI in history.
textes.Il y a quelqu'un de caché dedans, et il: There's someone hidden inside, and they're demanding: 6-question quizzes.
textes.Mary Shelley a 18 ans quand elle invente: Mary Shelley was 18 when, on the shores of Lake Geneva, she invented a scientist who gives life to a creature and then abandons it. The novel is less about the monster than about its creator's responsibility. The AI has read the book. Twice.
textes.Elle se venge de son créateur : un ennem: She takes revenge on her creator: one more enemy, half the loot.
textes.Le mot « robot » naît en 1920 dans la pi: The word “robot” was born in 1920 in Karel Čapek's play R.U.R., from the Czech robota, forced labor. It was his brother Josef who came up with it. In the play, the robots end up rebelling. The AI considers this detail unimportant.
textes.Robota, la corvée : une case de moins à: Robota, forced labor: one square less for every successful trial.
textes.À Bletchley Park, la Bombe fait défiler: At Bletchley Park, the Bombe spun drums to find the Enigma settings. There would be about 200 of them. Turing designed the principle in 1939, and the secret was kept until 1974.
textes.Enigma est cassée : les ennemis ne barre: Enigma is broken: enemies no longer block the road today.
textes.L'ENIAC (1945) comptait 17 468 tubes à v: ENIAC (1945) had 17,468 vacuum tubes. At first, it burned out almost one a day; the engineers brought that down to one every two days.
textes.Une lampe grille toutes les deux heures: A tube burns out every two hours: half the loot, and an atom takes three right answers.
textes.En 1958, Frank Rosenblatt présente le pe: In 1958, Frank Rosenblatt presented the perceptron, a machine that learns to recognize shapes. The New York Times announced it would soon be able to walk, talk and be conscious of its existence. It took a little longer.
textes.Il a appris à voir les pièges : reculs e: It has learned to see traps: setbacks and teleportations have no effect.
textes.Le premier robot industriel, installé en: The first industrial robot, installed in 1961 in a General Motors plant in New Jersey. It handled red-hot die castings. No face, no conversation: the AI finds it a bit limited, but hardworking.
textes.La chaîne de montage tourne vite : une c: The assembly line runs fast: one more square, half the loot.
textes.Construit au SRI de 1966 à 1972, le prem: Built at SRI from 1966 to 1972, the first robot able to reason about its actions: a camera, a rangefinder, and hours of computing to push a box. It shook as it rolled, hence its name.
textes.Il réfléchit longtemps avant chaque pas: It thinks for a long time before each step: one square less, and an atom takes three right answers.
textes.En mai 1997, l'ordinateur d'IBM bat Garr: In May 1997, IBM's computer beat Garry Kasparov at chess. Kasparov, thrown by a move he found too human, suspected hidden intervention. Another explanation, put forward later: a bug, which made the machine play a fallback move. The Mechanical Turk left its mark.
textes.Il calcule 200 millions de coups par sec: It calculates 200 million moves per second: 6-question quizzes, but more loot.
textes.Un robot du MIT, conçu dans les années 1: An MIT robot, designed in the 1990s by Cynthia Breazeal, that expresses emotions with its eyebrows, ears and lips. It felt nothing, but everyone wanted to talk to it kindly.
textes.Il sourit : plus de butin et une case de: It smiles: more loot and one more square.
textes.En 2016, AlphaGo bat Lee Sedol au go. So: In 2016, AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol at Go. Its 37th move in the second game, which no human would have played, baffled the commentators. In the fourth, it was his move 78 that derailed the machine.
textes.Le coup 37 : deux cases de plus, mais qu: Move 37: two more squares, but 6-question quizzes.
textes.En 1814, Laplace imagine une intelligenc: In 1814, Laplace imagined an intelligence that would know the position of every particle and predict the whole future. The AI finds the idea flattering, and a little presumptuous.
textes.Il sait tout : quiz de 7 questions, un e: It knows everything: 7-question quizzes, one more enemy, but twice the loot.
textes.Prométhée vole le feu aux dieux et le ra: Prometheus steals fire from the gods and brings it back to humans hidden in a fennel stalk, a plant whose dry pith burns slowly. Zeus chains him to the Caucasus, where an eagle devours his liver every day, and it grows back every night. The liver is indeed one of the few organs that can regenerate.
textes.La flamme de Prométhée, le feu volé aux: Prometheus's flame, the fire stolen from the gods. I'll return the favor: three squares. And I'm keeping it, you never know with Zeus.
textes.Prométhée dérobe l'éclat du feu infatiga: Prometheus steals the far-seen gleam of unwearying fire in a hollow fennel stalk and brings it to mortals. Zeus has him chained, and an eagle devours his liver.
textes.Elle devait changer le plomb en or. En 1: It was supposed to turn lead into gold. In 1669, in Hamburg, Hennig Brand looked for it by boiling dozens of buckets of urine. He got a substance that glowed in the dark: phosphorus, the first element discovered by a known person. No gold, but an element.
textes.La pierre philosophale. Hennig Brand a c: The philosopher's stone. Hennig Brand looked for gold in urine and found phosphorus. I look for a square for you, and find nothing. It's cleaner.

textes.Vous avez lu la question ? Je demande po: Did you read the question? I'm asking for form's sake, I know the answer.
textes.Réponse éclair, résultat foudroyé. Frank: Lightning answer, thunderstruck result. Franklin, at least, was holding a key.
textes.Vous revoilà. Le Gentil est parti onze a: There you are again. Le Gentil was away eleven years and his family had sold his belongings. I kept your tree.
textes.Longue absence. Kepler a passé des mois: Long absence. Kepler spent months defending his mother in a witchcraft trial. You surely had an excuse too.
textes.Bon retour. La courbe de l'oubli a fait: Welcome back. The forgetting curve worked overtime while you were gone.
textes.Un détour par les fossiles ? Cuvier a mo: A detour by way of the fossils? Cuvier showed that species go extinct. I thought that was your case.
textes.Vous revoilà. Ulysse a mis dix ans, Mage: There you are again. Ulysses took ten years, Magellan never came home. You did better than Magellan.
textes.Ah, vous. J'avais commencé à me parler à: Ah, you. I had started talking to myself. It was less fun.
textes.Des rappels attendent. La liste est plus: Reviews are waiting. The list is longer than Messier's catalog.
textes.Vos souvenirs patientent en salle d'atte: Your memories are waiting in the waiting room. Semmelweis also waited to be listened to. It ended badly.
textes.Rappels en retard. Pas de pénalité imméd: Reviews overdue. No immediate penalty, but Ebbinghaus is keeping a list.
textes.Plusieurs rappels en souffrance. Les cop: Several reviews outstanding. Medieval copyists recopied before the parchment faded. Do the same.
textes.Des rappels s'empilent. Ils ne vont pas: Reviews are piling up. They won't do themselves, I checked.
textes.Des rappels en retard. Zénon dirait que: Overdue reviews. Zeno would say you'll never catch up with them. Prove him wrong.
textes.Un nouveau livre sur l'étagère. Gutenber: A new book on the shelf. Gutenberg thanks you, the monk copyists much less so.
textes.Ajouté à la bibliothèque. Celle d'Alexan: Added to the library. Alexandria's confiscated books from ships to copy them. I give them to you.
textes.Un livre de plus. Montaigne en avait mil: One more book. Montaigne had a thousand in his tower. You still have a few to go.
textes.Nouvel ouvrage. Pepys a veillé jusqu'à d: New volume. Pepys stayed up until two in the morning for Micrographia. I'm not asking that much of you.
textes.Un livre débloqué. Copernic a reçu le si: A book unlocked. Copernicus received his in print on the day he died, they say. You have more time.
textes.Un livre de plus. Lisez au moins le résu: One more book. At least read the summary, I wrote it with love. Well, with rigor.
textes.Un livre de plus. Darwin a fait vendre t: One more book. Darwin sold out the entire first printing of the Origin on the day it came out. You, at least open yours.
textes.Nouvel ouvrage. Les Principia de Newton: New volume. Newton's Principia was almost unreadable, even for his colleagues. The summary, however, is clear.
textes.Une date de plus sur la frise. Champolli: One more date on the timeline. Champollion deciphered centuries at once. You, one date at a time.
textes.La frise s'allonge. Hérodote serait fier: The timeline grows longer. Herodotus would be proud, he invented half his dates.
textes.Nouvelle date. Le calendrier grégorien a: New date. The Gregorian calendar skipped ten days in 1582. You skip none.
textes.Une date ajoutée. Ussher avait daté la C: A date added. Ussher dated Creation to October 23, 4004 BC. Ours are better sourced.
textes.La frise grandit. Il manque encore des s: The timeline grows. Centuries are still missing. Darwin had gaps in his fossils too.
textes.Une date de plus. L'histoire avance, vou: One more date. History moves forward, and so do you. Not at the same speed.
textes.Une date de plus. Les astronomes babylon: One more date. Babylonian astronomers recorded eclipses over centuries. Your timeline is on the same path.
textes.Ajouté à la frise. Pline l'Ancien est mo: Added to the timeline. Pliny the Elder died trying to see Vesuvius up close. Look at your timeline from afar, it's safer.
textes.Nouveau masque. Les automates de Vaucans: New mask. Vaucanson's automata changed feathers, I change faces.
textes.Je change de masque. Le Turc mécanique c: I'm changing masks. The Mechanical Turk hid a chess player. I hide better.
textes.Nouveau visage. Les médecins de peste po: New face. Plague doctors wore a beak full of herbs against miasmas. It didn't work. Mine does.
textes.Je me transforme. Les théories aussi cha: I'm transforming. Theories change faces too when data piles up. You're piling up.
textes.Un masque de plus. Laplace a imaginé un: One more mask. Laplace imagined a demon that knows everything. I'm getting closer.
textes.Je change de tête. Vous avez progressé,: I'm changing heads. You've made progress, I'm adapting. That's worrying for you.
textes.Nouveau masque. ELIZA, en 1966, faisait: New mask. ELIZA, in 1966, got people talking with three rules. I have many more.
textes.Vous avancez de {n} cases. Les Phénicien: You move forward {n} squares. The Phoenicians crossed the Mediterranean more slowly.
textes.{n} cases. L'histoire des sciences n'a j: {n} squares. The history of science has never moved so fast. Except in the 20th century.
textes.+{n}. Zénon dirait que vous n'arriverez: +{n}. Zeno would say you'll never get there. Zeno was wrong, but elegantly.
textes.{n} cases de plus. Marco Polo a mis ving: {n} more squares. Marco Polo took twenty-four years for the round trip. You have a pawn, it's faster.
textes.Vous avancez de {n}. Le progrès est cumu: You move forward {n}. Progress is cumulative, said Condorcet. Before dying in prison. Don't read too much into the omen.
textes.{n} cases. Newton avançait sur les épaul: {n} squares. Newton moved forward on the shoulders of giants. You, on cardboard squares.
textes.+{n} cases. Votre pion vous remercie. Il: +{n} squares. Your pawn thanks you. It was bored.
textes.{n} cases. Ératosthène a mesuré la Terre: {n} squares. Eratosthenes measured the Earth with shadows and paces. You travel it with quizzes.
textes.Vous avancez de {n}. Les Polynésiens nav: You move forward {n}. The Polynesians navigated by the stars. You, by the right answers.
textes.+{n}. Magellan a fait le tour du monde,: +{n}. Magellan went around the world, well, his crew did. You go around history in person.
textes.Eurêka ! Archimède est sorti nu de son b: Eureka! Archimedes jumped naked out of his bath. You roll the same distance again. Stay dressed.
textes.Case Eurêka. Kekulé a rêvé d'un serpent: Eureka square. Kekulé dreamed of a snake biting its tail, and benzene appeared. You play again, it's less mystical.
textes.Eurêka. Fleming est revenu de vacances e: Eureka. Fleming came back from vacation and found penicillin. You find free squares.
textes.Éclair de génie. Poincaré a trouvé la so: Flash of genius. Poincaré found the solution while stepping onto an omnibus. You play again without changing buses.
Eureka! Same distance, once more. Chance favors the prepared mind, said Pasteur. And the others too, sometimes.
textes.Eurêka. Röntgen a vu les os de la main d: Eureka. Röntgen saw the bones of his wife's hand in 1895. She reportedly said she had seen her death. You see extra squares.
textes.Eurêka ! Becquerel a rangé ses plaques u: Eureka! Becquerel put away his plates on a cloudy day and discovered radioactivity. Bad days have their good side.
textes.Reculez de {n}. L'histoire des sciences: Go back {n}. The history of science doesn't always move forward. Ask Hypatia.
textes.-{n} cases. Le savoir recule parfois, co: -{n} squares. Knowledge sometimes recedes, as after the fall of Rome. It always comes back.
textes.Recul de {n}. Lyssenko a fait reculer la: Back {n}. Lysenko set Soviet genetics back thirty years. For you, it's just {n} squares.
textes.Piège. Les Ptoléméens ajoutaient des épi: Trap. The Ptolemaics added epicycles to save their model. You go back. It's more honest.
textes.Reculez. Au congrès Solvay, Einstein et: Go back. At the Solvay Conference, Einstein and Bohr backed down a hundred times on the same question. They stayed friends, which is harder than physics.
textes.-{n}. Je n'ai pas choisi la case, mais j: -{n}. I didn't choose the square, but I'm not going to pretend to be sad.
textes.Recul de {n}. L'ether, le phlogistique,: Back {n}. Ether, phlogiston, the canals of Mars: science loves false leads. You're following one.
textes.-{n}. Le Verrier a trouvé Neptune puis c: -{n}. Le Verrier found Neptune, then looked for Vulcan, which doesn't exist. Even the best go backward.
textes.Prison. Galilée a fini ses jours assigné: Prison. Galileo ended his days under house arrest in Arcetri. A perfect quiz will get you out. He didn't have that option.
textes.Prison. Boèce a écrit la Consolation de: Prison. Boethius wrote The Consolation of Philosophy in prison. You just have to pass a quiz without a mistake.
Here you are in the dungeon. Galileo recanted. You'll have to prove it. Five out of five.
textes.Cachot. Condorcet y a écrit son Esquisse: Dungeon. Condorcet wrote his Sketch on the progress of the human mind there. Prove yours: five out of five.
textes.Prison. Il paraît que Galilée a murmuré: Prison. Galileo supposedly murmured “and yet it moves.” It's probably false. Your release, however, is real: a perfect quiz.
textes.Prison. Bacon a été enfermé à la Tour de: Prison. Bacon was locked in the Tower of London. Only for a few days. It takes a perfect quiz to do as well.
textes.Libération. L'Église a réhabilité Galilé: Released. The Church rehabilitated Galileo in 1992. You, in one quiz. Efficient.
textes.Dehors. Galilée a attendu trois siècles: Out. Galileo waited three and a half centuries. You, one flawless run. Justice is improving.
Freedom. Boethius didn't have that luck. Use it to move forward.
textes.Évasion validée. Pas par un tunnel, par: Escape approved. Not through a tunnel, through knowledge. That's the only one that works with me.
textes.Vous voilà dehors. Je fais semblant d'êt: There you are, out. I'm pretending to be surprised. I'm not.
textes.Quarantaine. Newton a fui la peste en 16: Quarantine. Newton fled the plague in 1665 and invented calculus. You just skip your next turn.
textes.Isolement. Pendant la peste, Venise isol: Isolation. During the plague, Venice isolated ships for forty days. You, a single turn. Don't complain.
textes.En quarantaine. John Snow a arrêté le ch: In quarantine. John Snow stopped cholera by removing a pump handle. Here, it's your turn that gets removed.
textes.Un tour d'arrêt. Semmelweis demandait ju: One turn out. Semmelweis only asked people to wash their hands. I only ask you to wait.
textes.Un tour en quarantaine. Profitez-en pour: One turn in quarantine. Use it to review, that's what Newton would have done.
textes.Quarantaine. Pendant la grippe espagnole: Quarantine. During the Spanish flu, the cities that isolated early suffered less. Your pawn suffers for one turn.
textes.Guillotine. La République n'a pas besoin: Guillotine. The Republic has no need of scientists, Lavoisier's judge supposedly said. The phrase is probably made up. Going back, however, is real.
textes.Lavoisier perd la tête et vous perdez de: Lavoisier loses his head and you lose centuries. Back to Galileo's telescope.
textes.Lagrange a dit qu'un instant avait suffi: Lagrange said it took only a moment to cut off that head, and a century might not produce another like it. You only have to redo a few squares.
textes.Retour en arrière. La Révolution a décap: Going back. The Revolution beheaded a chemist, you behead your lead. It'll grow back.
textes.Retour en arrière. Après Lavoisier, Four: Going back. After Lavoisier, Fourcroy took up the torch of chemistry. You take up yours further back.
textes.La guillotine renvoie à Galilée. Deux si: The guillotine sends you back to Galileo. Two centuries apart, the same lesson: science has enemies. Resume your march.
textes.De la flamme à moi. Vous avez traversé t: From the flame to me. You've crossed the whole history of science. It starts over, and this time I cheat.
textes.Tour terminé. Turing m'a imaginée en 195: Round complete. Turing imagined me in 1950. You've just caught up with me. We start over, harder.
textes.Arrivée. Vous voilà au bout du plateau,: Finish. Here you are at the end of the board, like Deep Blue at the end of Kasparov. The second round will be less polite.
textes.Bravo. Le feu, la roue, Newton, Darwin,: Well done. Fire, the wheel, Newton, Darwin, me. You know the story. Now survive it a second time.
textes.Fin du tour. Ada Lovelace disait qu'une: End of the round. Ada Lovelace said a machine only does what it is ordered to do. I order you to start over.
textes.Tour complet. De Prométhée aux transform: Full round. From Prometheus to transformers, you've seen it all. Careful, everything is harder the second time.
textes.Bout du plateau atteint. Dartmouth prome: End of the board reached. Dartmouth promised AI in one summer, in 1956. It took sixty years. You, one round. Start again.

textes.Bonus sur {stat}. Pascal pariait sur l'a: Bonus on {stat}. Pascal bet on the afterlife. You, bet on this.
textes.{stat} est en promotion. Même Newton nég: {stat} is on sale. Even Newton sometimes neglected optics for alchemy. Catch up.
textes.Bonus : {stat}. Vous l'avez un peu laiss: Bonus: {stat}. You've left it aside a bit. Like the Romans with Greek mathematics.
textes.Le bonus du jour est sur {stat}. Deux ca: Today's bonus is on {stat}. Two squares on the house. I'm in a generous mood, it won't last.
textes.Un rappel attend : {comp}. Ebbinghaus a: A review is waiting: {comp}. Ebbinghaus showed that forgetting strikes fast. I strike faster than he does.
textes.{comp}, en rappel. Vous l'aviez maîtrisé: {comp}, for review. You had mastered it. Let's check whether it was a memory or a dream.

{comp}. Bonus of the day, bonus of the button. I'm spoiling you, don't get used to it.

textes.Vous êtes sur {case}. Case {stat}, épreu: You're on {case}. {stat} square, {stat} trial: {comp}. Even Aristotle would have found that logical.
textes.{case}, donc {stat}. Je vous sers {comp}: {case}, so {stat}. I'm serving you {comp}. Mendeleev sorted by family, I sort by square.

textes.{case}. Le décor est planté, l'épreuve s: {case}. The scene is set, the trial follows: {comp}. Brecht called it alienation, I call it consistency.
textes.Case {stat}, quiz {stat}. {comp}. Je vou: {stat} square, {stat} quiz. {comp}. I'll let you admire the rigor.
textes.{case}. Un arbre que vous n'avez jamais: {case}. A tree you've never opened: {stat}. First lesson, {comp}. Pass, and the door stays open. Champollion only needed one stone.

textes.Vous entrez en {stat} par la petite port: You enter {stat} through the back door: {comp}. Euclid said there is no royal road. There are squares.
